#1947. Young Hammer is ‘big money flop’ according to report – but West Ham fans won’t agree

In these days of instant access to everything, fame is sudden and success is apparently supposed to happen overnight. Criticism of West Ham’s team and their mid-table mediocrity is often swift and harsh. Even players who arrived in the summer are already being written off, according to supporters and news sites.

Which seems especially harsh considering the age and trajectory of several key players in this West Ham side.

How many ‘West Ham legends’ of the past would have been discarded after their first dozen games, I wonder, if they’d not been an immediate sensation.

Bad enough that so-called ‘fans’ took to booing Scott Parker’s very first home game at 90 minutes: Now it seems one of the youngest talents from the summer intake is already being labelled as a  ‘flop’.

That’s the flavour of a report out this evening from givemesport.com who claim that:

As they take aim at ..Edwin Austbø who, at just twenty one, has hardly had a chance to get settled in east London before he’s being labelled a’ big money’ (eh?) flop, despite his transfer fee being a modest £11 million. Perspective being everything, that’s about a quarter of a Kilman who cost £40 million and would surely be most people’s choice for the ‘big money flop’ label.

A flop? After three months? With two goals and two assists at just 21 years of age, I’d say Austbo is well on track to grow into the team.

“Expectations were also high that summer signing Austbo could prove to be an exciting addition in the second tier this term….He has two goals and two assists for the Irons so far this term, but you would probably expect his goal contribution numbers to be higher in a team which has scored 38 league goals…..

As things stand, Austbo is quickly becoming a big-money transfer flop, and he needs to improve quickly to start repaying his fee.”

Steady on, guys, This young man has huge talent, was not outrageously expensive and has already produced more goals and assists than players who cost twice his transfer fee. At least wait until the end of the season – his first in the English leagues – before writing him off.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

Been thinking the same, about former greats not being given a chance today, due to constant demands for success and questionable expectations. Expectations, hopes, ambitions, all normal, but with any sport, you also need to be a bit of a fatalist I think and not expect it to happen tomorrow.

Look at Frank Lampard Snr, LB for 18 seasons and coming from the youth system, capped twice for England. 100% a club great who won trophies with WHU. Happened, because he was given plenty of chances to develop as a youth because he’ll have had bad games, maybe an occasional below-par season (normal unless you are Declan Rice) before everything clicked.

Current WHU team youngsters need their to chance to develop in the same way, because we have plenty of youngsters in and around the 1st team who have the potential to develop and become successful players. With the likes of Herrick, Golambeckis, Engels, Magassa, Mayers, Cummings, Fearon…. (there are too many!!) WHU team has a lot of potential – just add some savvy recruitment along the way.

For this to happen need a longer term sense of ambition (something DK & Koppen might well have) as opposed to short-term, but brief want for success. Too early for this team as it is a young team needing to develop before becoming reliable. Might be worth the wait though, because there is a lot of talent there and a burgeoning recruitment team.

Written without considering what they were saying. Austbo is yet to prove himself at West Ham, but hasn’t performed too badly, considering that he has not had a regular or consistent run in the team. Give him a chance.

We’ve more to worry about than a player with 4 goal contributions in the minutes played equivalent of 4.5 games!! .. If he keeps that ratio up, I’d be more worried about keeping hold of him than calling him an expensive flop!!! .. His direct competition for a place is Solomon who has 4 goal contributions in the minutes played equivalent of 11 games! .. I know the name I’d have on my team sheet and he’d be playing the whole game .. Whilst looking at these ratios, Kante has 5 goal contributions in the minutes played equivalent of 8 games, which might improve if he’s given license to run forward into space and where he can’t lose the ball in dangerous positions .. #1946. Arsenal transfer dilemma: Alex Scott and Nico Paz could force difficult decisions for Arteta

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Potential signings of Alex Scott and Nico Paz may pose a challenge for Arteta.

While both players would add quality to the squad, their arrival would be a consideration for current players in the Emirates squad.

Scott would add quality in midfield, and Paz adds creativity and versatility going forward. Arteta must consider that adding these players may hinder the development of current players.

Arsenal are believed to be keen on bringing Alex Scott to the club.

After rejecting contract offers from Bournemouth, Scott could only have one year left on his contract at the club next summer. However, he is understood to be valued by Bournemouth at over £100m.

He would be a great addition for Arteta, with the versatility and skill he has. He could give added competition in midfield.

Yet his potential arrival raises questions about Myles Lewis-Skelly’s future role.

Myles Lewis-Skelly was included in the Champions League final line-up last season. He showed that he is trusted by the club.He has also demonstrated his commitment by remaining at the club despite opportunities to gain regular playing time at other clubs.

Signing another expensive midfielder may present difficulties. It is unclear at this point whether Scott will be a useful addition to the squad or simply overcrowd this area of the team.

Nico Paz presents another interesting option for Arsenal.

Paz joined Como from Real Madrid in the summer. He has caught the eye of a number of big clubs and has increased his appeal with strong performances in international football. The 22-year-old has scored 5 times in his last 5 games for Argentina.

Paz is a versatile right-sided player and could be an appealing addition to Arteta’s strike force.

There are already plenty of players fighting for attacking positions at Arsenal.

Bukayo Saka is key in the team’s attack, and with Martin Ødegaard and Noni Madueke in the squad too, there are plenty of options. Max Dowman is a young player looking to break into the first team.

While Paz would add quality to the squad, Arsenal would need to find a specific role for him. There are complications with the move, though. Real Madrid have an option to re-sign him in 2027 for 80 million euros.

Although Arsenal are facing challenges in attracting quality players to the club. They now also face issues in managing a squad with experienced internationals and developing young players.

Although Scott and Paz would improve the depth of the squad, players must not be sacrificed for new players if they have already shown quality.

Players such as Lewis-Skelly and Dowman may be negatively affected by this. Opportunities may be taken away from them if the club continues to spend large amounts of money on new players.

However, it is still very important for Arsenal to bring in quality players to compete for major titles.

Know how the additions will integrate within the playing style and how they affect the other players within the squad.

The Gunners can strengthen further without overloading the squad. Good additions can be made to the first XI whilst also providing a realistic chance for young players to come through from within the academy.

Back in July, Kyle Healy-Matthews was tempted away from West Ham by Newcastle United.

The highly teenage starlet was a young player the Hammers were desperate not to lose.

Newcastle United fighting off a number of other Premier League clubs who had been competing to attract the teenage right-back.

However, personal terms were agreed between NUFC and Kyle Healy-Matthews and the deal completed

Obviously one for the future he looked a very positive addition, the young right-back is quick and with very good defensive ability, he’d been a stand out player in the West Ham young set-up.

Since the October 2021 takeover, Newcastle United having signed a lot of promising young players from other clubs, which will hopefully pay longer-term benefits.

Now Newcastle United have revealed on Wednesday morning that Kyle Healy-Matthews has signed his first professional contract with the club on his 17th birthday.

Official Newcastle United media stating: ‘The Romford-born youngster joined Newcastle’s Academy from West Ham United last summer and initially linked up with Chris Moore’s Under-18s squad as a first-year scholar before agreeing professional terms with the Magpies. Healy-Matthews, who primarily plays as a right-back, expressed his delight in committing his future with Newcastle and has relished his time at United’s Little Benton Academy to date.’

Kyle Healy-Matthews: “I’m very pleased to sign my first professional contract,” he told newcastleunited.com. “It’s a special moment for myself and my family, seeing all the hard work which has led up to this. Newcastle is a massive club with goals and ambitions that I feel I can contribute in. I believe I can play a big part for this club. I’ve enjoyed my time here a lot. I’ve had a lot of support from my peers and coaches with helping me to settle in as well as progressing along the way.”

The official NUFC media going on to say: ‘Kyle Healy-Matthews, who cites fellow right-back Kyle Walker as his footballing idol, has made a positive start to the current campaign at Under-18 level, with the Toon teenagers winning six of their opening seven league matches and currently occupying third spot in the division. The rapid full-back believes he has handled the challenge of relocating hundreds of miles away from home for the first time and is determined to advance through the Magpies’ youth ranks. Healy-Matthews, a member of West Ham’s Under-17 Premier League Cup winning side last season.’

Kyle Healy-Matthews: “I’ve only been here for a few months but I think I can say the move has paid off. Moving very far away from home could have been tricky but with all of the support I had around me from my peers, that really helped me to settle in quickly. I’m loving my time with the Under-18s. This season, my main aim is to progress into the Under-21s and long-term, but hopefully not too long, would be to progress into the first-team.”

Steve Harper is Newcastle United Academy Director: “Kyle has made an excellent impression since joining the Academy in the summer and we’re pleased to see him rewarded with his first professional contract. Moving away from home and settling into a new environment can be a significant challenge for any young player but Kyle has handled the transition brilliantly. He’s worked extremely hard since arriving at the club and his attitude, commitment and willingness to learn have stood out throughout his time here so far. This contract is recognition of the progress he’s made, and we’re excited to continue supporting his development as he takes the next steps in his career at Newcastle United.”

There will be no live UK television coverage of Chelsea’s return to Premier League action against Bournemouth on Saturday afternoon.

Xabi Alonso’s side host the Cherries at Stamford Bridge in a traditional 3pm kick-off, with the fixture falling within the Saturday afternoon broadcasting blackout.

That means supporters unable to attend will need to follow the match through other channels, rather than watching it live on Sky Sports or TNT Sports.

Although the game will not be televised live in the UK, supporters can follow developments through the official Chelsea website and the Premier League website.

Chelsea will then turn their attention to a trip to Everton on Saturday, 17 October, with that fixture scheduled for a 12.30pm kick-off at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

#1943. Max Dowman’s Arsenal return: Is the teenage star one to watch, and can he keep his nose clean?

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Max Dowman shortly returns to action for Arsenal after serving a three-game suspension.

His absence has been disappointing, but the experience should give the youngster an important lesson. Can he put the incident behind him and show Mikel Arteta that he can be trusted?

Dowman received a red card against Fleetwood Town after kicking out at Harrison Neal. Arsenal appealed the decision, but the FA rejected the club’s appeal.

The suspension ruled him out of three domestic fixtures against Liverpool, Hull City and Newcastle United.

He’ll be back on 29 November as Arsenal take on Manchester City. This should give the young star a chance to get his season back on track and showcase what makes him such a highly-rated player.

Dowman looks very promising for the future. He has shown great adaptability playing with the more experienced players and has the self-belief to make an impact in games.

He has performed well in the Carabao Cup. In the 4-2 win against Ipswich, Dowman scored two goals, showing his flair and poise in front of goal.

Arteta has given him opportunities to play in the Premier League and Champions League, meaning that he appears to have a clear route into the first team.

Although Dowman still has a lot to learn, he displays great potential in his technical ability and combative nature. As he gets more games under his belt, fans will be excited to see how he progresses.

Dowman was sent off in an unfortunate moment. He was heavily challenged by Neal and, after lashing out, was shown a straight red card.

Although this one moment should not be enough to dismiss a young player from the game completely, it can serve as a valuable lesson on the pressure that comes with playing at a higher level.

Opponents will test Dowman physically, but he must learn to keep his composure. As he starts making an impact, some players may target his age and inexperience to unsettle him.

As he gets more game time, consistency will be key. Arteta must be confident that Dowman can be relied on in high pressure situations.

Arsenal do not need to rush Dowman into the first team. The squad’s quality allows Arteta to manage his minutes and give him time to develop without putting too much pressure on him.

If Dowman is to play against Manchester City, it will depend on Arteta’s plans, but he has certainly done enough to warrant consideration.

The suspension should not define his season. What matters now is how he responds, both on and off the pitch.

Dowman has the talent to become an important player for Arsenal. Keeping his discipline will be just as important as displaying his ability.

#1942. Chelsea’s interest in Alex Scott remains despite Bournemouth transfer stance

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Bournemouth’s determination to keep Alex Scott has done little to discourage Chelsea, who remain among the leading contenders to sign the England midfielder.

The Blues had a £64m bid rejected during the summer, but their interest has continued into the new season. According to Matt Law of The Telegraph, Chelsea are at the front of the queue of clubs monitoring the 23-year-old.

Bournemouth, however, have no intention of allowing Scott to leave in January. talkSPORT reported this week that the south coast club remain determined to retain him, despite his reluctance to sign a contract extension.

Scott’s current deal runs until 2028, leaving Bournemouth with time to negotiate, although their position could become more complicated if no agreement is reached before next summer.

The midfielder’s immediate priority is recovering from a thigh injury sustained while representing England. He impressed during the 7-0 Nations League victory over Croatia but was withdrawn after 70 minutes. Subsequent examinations revealed a quadriceps problem, with BBC Sport reporting that he could miss six to eight weeks.

His absence is a setback for Bournemouth, who have relied heavily on the former Bristol City midfielder this season. It also introduces another consideration for clubs monitoring his progress ahead of the January window.

Chelsea are not alone in their admiration. Arsenal and Liverpool have also been linked with Scott, whose performances have attracted attention beyond the Premier League.

Suggestions circulating on social media that Bournemouth have already agreed to let him leave in January remain unsubstantiated. There has been no reliable confirmation of such an arrangement, and the club’s reported position is firmly against a winter sale.

For Chelsea, the more realistic opportunity may come next summer, particularly if Scott continues to resist signing a new contract.

#1941. Arsenal fan quizzes Graham Scott on why Newcastle United goal not disallowed

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Graham Scott has been quizzed by an Arsenal fan as to why Malick Thiaw’s goal was allowed to stand on Saturday.

That goal put Newcastle United 2-1 up on 62 minutes.

Graham Scott refereed in the Premier League for a decade and he was also a video assistant referee (VAR) more than 100 times.

Now retired, he brings his unique insight into how match officials operate for The Athletic.

They invite readers to send in questions each week for Graham Scott to answer.

This week the former top referee received this one from an Arsenal fan…

‘Why did neither the referee nor VAR penalise the holding on Jurrien Timber that allowed Dan Burn to win a free header to create Newcastle’s second goal against Arsenal?’

Graham Scott explaining: “Timber was impeded by Will Osula as he chased after Burn (circled below). Osula was impeded by Declan Rice, who was holding him with both arms. Malick Thiaw was being held by Martin Odegaard, who was being held by Thiaw. Lewis Miley blocked Ezri Konsa, who pulled Miley to get past him. There were probably other potential fouls, too. The officials look for the most serious offences that have the greatest impact, and none of these came close to meeting those thresholds — which are set by the league and the lawmakers, not the refs.”

I know that no football fan takes it well when any decision goes against them BUT as a group I think Arsenal fans do appear especially bizarre in terms of not willing to accept any decision that doesn’t go their way.

Graham Scott was also asked another question regarding Saturday’s game…

‘When David Raya went down for treatment the first time at Newcastle on Saturday, why did another Arsenal player not have to leave the field for a minute? I thought that was the new rule.’

Graham Scott: ‘No Arsenal player was asked to leave the field for a minute because Raya had collided with an opponent and requested treatment at the earliest opportunity. There is a similar exemption if a goalkeeper’s injury occurs from a foul that the referee deems worthy of a yellow or red card. This rule was introduced to stop goalkeepers mysteriously sitting down and demanding treatment for fictitious muscle injuries while their coach held an impromptu time-out chat with the rest of the team.’

I have to confess, I totally forgot about this new rule coming in. Has any goalkeeper got ‘injured’ this season and had treatment on the pitch which led to his Premier League side going down to ten men for a minute with an outfield player going off?

#1940. Portsmouth v West Ham Preview: Predicted XI As Parker Searches For First Win

Portsmouth v West Ham United EFL Championship, Fratton Park, Tuesday 24 November 2026, 7.45pm GMT

This is a crucial match for West Ham and Scott Parker, who has probably endured the shortest honeymoon period of any Hammers manager in recent memory. His first three games have produced a rousing comeback against Cardiff City, a forgettable defeat at Blackburn Rovers and Saturday’s frustrating 1-1 draw with Preston North End.

West Ham dominated possession and registered 30 attempts against Preston, yet never really looked clinical enough to score the winner. Indeed, had the referee awarded another 20 minutes of injury time, I’m still not convinced we would have found a second goal.

Parker is still waiting for his first victory as West Ham head coach, and Tuesday’s trip to Fratton Park represents another difficult assignment. Portsmouth have lost just once in eight Championship matches and sit only one point and two places behind the tenth-placed Hammers.

Ordinarily, one might expect Parker to do some tinkering after failing to beat the team at the bottom of the division. However, I suspect he won’t make sweeping changes because he was very pleased with the way his team performed against Preston.

Edson Alvarez – likely to become key in Parker’s plans this season

Parker said he got almost everything he wanted from the performance apart from the result, while describing Finlay Herrick and Edson Álvarez as “brilliant” in his post-match assessment. I’m not quite sure I would agree with that overall verdict, although the return of Álvarez was unquestionably a bonus.

The Mexican looked decent on his return to the team and provided some much-needed protection in front of the back four. Parker has probably made it clear that, for the remainder of this season, West Ham will play with a recognised holding midfielder.

Without wishing to sound like a scratched record, I still believe Jarrod Bowen needs to be used more centrally. Parker appeared to have been given the keys to unlocking West Ham’s attacking potential against Cardiff, but unfortunately he seems to have kept them in his back pocket ever since.

Bowen remains our most dangerous attacking player, yet watching him pinned to the right flank against Preston was depressing. West Ham lacked magic, invention and somebody willing to take responsibility in the areas where matches are won.

Mohamadou Kanté can consider himself unlucky not to have featured at all against Preston because he has been one of West Ham’s better players this season. There is an argument for playing him in the attacking midfield position at Portsmouth, where his pace and direct running could give Parker’s team something different.

However, I don’t think Parker will throw the baby out with the bathwater. He has already spoken about remaining stable and consistent, so I expect Divine Mukasa to retain his place behind Joël Piroe.

Piroe should continue up front, as much because of the lack of convincing alternatives as anything else. Manor Solomon could return on the left, with Parker perhaps deciding that his experience is better suited to a difficult night at Fratton Park.

I suspect there will be a change at left-back, with Ollie Scarles coming into the team. Max Kilman is available again after completing his one-match suspension and should immediately return alongside Konstantinos Mavropanos.

According to the club’s official team news, Alphonse Areola and Kyle Walker-Peters continue to be assessed. Unless Walker-Peters is unexpectedly declared fit, Joël Veltman should remain at right-back.

Portsmouth possess a worse attack than West Ham but a better defence, so this is unlikely to be an open game. They are only two places and one point behind us, while their recent results suggest Parker’s team will have to work extremely hard for anything at Fratton Park.

West Ham’s failure to convert possession into goals remains the obvious concern. However, if Parker can keep things tight defensively and finally find a way to make one of our attacking opportunities count, I believe the Hammers can edge it.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

No to Kilman, it’s been proven so many times we are better without him. I don’t understand why we keep going back to him, maybe its his price tag. I do however agree with using Bowen differently.

The only thing I’m asking is that we rewrite the script for once, do not go behind, then spend the rest of the match chasing the game. There’s only so many times that script can play out isn’t there ? It’s been like Groundhog Day.

Herrick was OK give him another shot, Alvarez a lot better than OK essential starter, Mayers not Scarles please, and give Piroe a run of games as he looks the best of not particularly inspiring options.

#1939. Arsenal transfer news: Why Kevin Schade could be a smart January signing

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal are looking to strengthen their attacking options in January. One player they are reportedly keeping an eye on is Brentford winger Kevin Schade. Mikel Arteta will be keen to add competition in attack, and Schade may be a good option.

Schade will give additional pace to the offence. He is capable of playing in multiple attacking positions to provide Arteta with extra depth in the squad.

However, it may be difficult to get Schade. He is on loan at Brentford, and may want to keep him in the long term. If Schade is seen as a key player in the future, they may be difficult to negotiate with.

Schade’s versatility is another big plus. His speed and straightforward method make him hard to deal with for defenders. In addition, he can be used as a left-sided attacker, giving Arteta more flexibility in his front line. As the club are playing in a number of competitions, this can be very useful.

Schade has already scored 3 times in the Premier League this season. He has quickly adapted to playing in England after moving from Freiburg to Brentford in 2023.

Despite only being 24 years old, Schade still has a lot to improve on. He has lots of experience in the Premier League but has not quite reached the peak of his ability yet. If he moves to Arsenal, he may be able to elevate his performance.

Brentford has already started negotiations with Schade regarding a contract extension that would keep him tied to the club for a long time. He is already contracted until the summer of 2028.

Arsenal’s interest could prove problematic. Other clubs are also keeping their eyes on this player. Tottenham in particular are not seen as a major threat at this stage.

It is going to be very challenging for Brentford to let go of Schade because he has played a key part in their offensive setup, and losing Schade could prove disastrous.

Arsenal will have to pay Brentford whatever they ask for, Schade, and since he has a decent amount of time left on his contract, Brentford has an edge in negotiations.

Arsenal’s interest in Schade is logical. His versatility will provide Arteta with additional flexibility because of his prior experience in the Premier League.

It can be considered positive to sign new strikers. Arsenal must decide if they believe that Schade will fit in well with their current players and whether the asking price from Brentford is reasonable.

As of now, there are no signs of a transfer on the horizon, but it is clear that Schade is a player worth monitoring as the winter transfer window approaches.

Chelsea have reportedly made contact with Palmeiras as they attempt to gain an early advantage in the race to sign Brazilian teenager Eduardo Conceicao.

The 16-year-old forward has attracted attention from several leading European clubs, but Chelsea are understood to be among the first to establish direct contact with Palmeiras over a potential future transfer.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, the London club have held a series of discussions as they seek to position themselves ahead of their rivals.

Palmeiras are reportedly preparing for substantial offers, with some figures at the Brazilian club discussing a valuation as high as €100m (£85m).

That figure has not been established as a firm asking price, however, and Brus reports that industry sources expect the eventual cost to be lower. Chelsea’s previous investment of approximately £51m in Estevao is regarded as a possible benchmark.

Manchester City’s ownership group have also made contact regarding Conceicao, while Arsenal, Manchester United, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain are among the clubs reported to have watched him.

Chelsea’s existing relationship with Palmeiras could help their efforts, although the level of competition means there is no guarantee that their early interest will lead to a deal.

The player’s age is another consideration. Conceicao cannot complete an international transfer to England until he turns 18, leaving interested clubs facing a potentially lengthy wait before he can join their squads.

Chelsea have already demonstrated their willingness to agree deals for young players well before they are eligible to arrive, with Estevao providing a particularly relevant example.

No formal bid or agreement has been reported for Conceicao. Nevertheless, the latest claims suggest Chelsea are prepared to explore another long-term investment in Brazilian talent rather than wait until the player becomes available for an immediate move.

#1937. Chelsea news: Stewart departure, Scott interest and Bournemouth preparations

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Chelsea’s sporting department is facing another change following news of Laurence Stewart’s impending departure, while the club continue to be linked with potential additions to their squad.

Alex Scott and Palmeiras teenager Eduardo Conceicao have both featured in Thursday’s transfer coverage, with Xabi Alonso also preparing his players for Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth.

Here is our 7pm round-up of the latest Chelsea news for Thursday, 8 October.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club planning to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

His departure is understood to be amicable and will not take immediate effect. Stewart joined from Monaco in 2022, initially as technical director, before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley.

As detailed in our report on Stewart’s departure and Chelsea’s leadership reshuffle, Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields are expected to take on expanded responsibilities across recruitment, player development and the wider BlueCo operation.

The changes follow discussions about the club’s sporting structure that reportedly began earlier this year. There is no confirmed suggestion that Stewart’s departure resulted from a disagreement with Alonso.

Chelsea’s reported interest in Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott remains a talking point, despite the south coast club’s determination to retain the England international.

The Blues reportedly had a £64m offer rejected during the summer, with Matt Law of The Telegraph subsequently identifying Chelsea as leading contenders for the 23-year-old.

However, as examined in our latest report on Chelsea’s interest in Scott, Bournemouth are not expected to entertain a January sale.

Scott’s immediate concern is recovering from a thigh injury suffered while representing England. The midfielder could face several weeks on the sidelines, potentially complicating Bournemouth’s plans as well as any future discussions about his next move.

Chelsea have also reportedly made contact with Palmeiras over 16-year-old forward Eduardo Conceicao, who is attracting attention from several leading European clubs.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, Chelsea have held discussions with the Brazilian club as they explore the possibility of a future deal.

Our report on Chelsea’s interest in Eduardo Conceicao explains that a valuation as high as €100m has been suggested, although that figure is not a confirmed asking price or evidence of a formal bid.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Real Madrid are among the other clubs reportedly monitoring the teenager. Conceicao would be unable to complete a transfer to England until he turns 18, making any prospective move a longer-term consideration.

Alonso’s attention will now turn to Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

The match kicks off at 3pm and will not be televised live in the United Kingdom because of the Saturday afternoon broadcasting blackout.

Our Chelsea v Bournemouth kick-off and how-to-watch guide provides the full details, including how to follow the match and the available overseas broadcast information.

Scott’s injury is expected to deprive Bournemouth of an important midfield option, although Chelsea will have their own fitness decisions to make as players return from international duty.

After Saturday’s fixture, Chelsea travel to Hill Dickinson Stadium to face Everton on 17 October. Alonso will be looking for greater consistency as the domestic programme resumes.

#1936. Newcastle vs Arsenal: Team news, predicted line-ups and match preview

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal will have a tough task on hand as they visit St James’ Park.

Mikel Arteta’s side are five points clear at the top of the Premier League after their 1-0 victory over Hull City ahead of the international break. The Gunners have now gone nine games unbeaten in all competitions.

Despite only one win in their last six games, Newcastle will be a dangerous side at home.

Although Arsenal have won the last three encounters with Newcastle, recent games at Tyneside have not gone entirely smoothly for Mikel Arteta. He will also have to make a few key decisions in the squad with players injured and a busy run of fixtures.

Bruno Guimaraes will certainly be a topic of discussion for this game. The midfielder joined Newcastle four-and-a-half years ago, playing an important role in the development of the side, before moving to Arsenal on a reported 75 million pound move in the summer.

Whilst he has struggled to make himself an automatic starter in Arteta’s side, he could have a bigger impact with the absence of Martin Zubimendi.

Zubimendi is likely to be out for several weeks. Declan Rice should start, and Guimaraes is also likely to be involved, to form a double pivot.

Newcastle will try to play a gritty game to unsettle Arsenal. Despite Guimaraes’ knowledge of the opposition, he will have to assist the visitors to maintain control of the midfield battle.

Saliba is now back in contention after recovering from a back injury. The Frenchman has not played in the first team this season, but has made two appearances as he recovers. He played 45 minutes for the U21s.

Arteta confirmed that Saliba is in good shape and will begin to play more games, though he is unlikely to be in the starting line-up for the game against Newcastle.

Konsa should be in the starting line-up alongside Gabriel. Saliba could come on from the bench, as he looks to make his first competitive appearance of the season after the Champions League final last time out.

Saka is still unavailable due to quad trouble, whilst Dowman is suspended. Madueke should start on the right and Havertz will spearhead the attack.

Newcastle United: Predicted line-up not confirmed in the supplied team news.

Arsenal: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes; Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz.

Arsenal absentees: Martin Zubimendi, Bukayo Saka and Max Dowman.

Saliba is available but is not expected to start.

Newcastle have leaked goals at home this season. However, with Madueke and Tzolis providing pace in wide areas, this should not worry Arsenal too much.

Nevertheless, this game should be challenging for the Gunners. Newcastle are dangerous in attack and can capitalise on errors quickly in possession.

Despite Arsenal’s solid defensive record, they have failed to keep a clean sheet in their 4 visits to St James’ Park.

Overall this should be a good watch with goals scored by both sides. However, Arsenal should be able to pick up some vital 3 points.

Predicted score: Newcastle United 2-3 Arsenal.

#1935. Saudi Arabia PIF have now put 25 per cent of Newcastle United up for sale

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Breaking news on Wednesday that the Saudi Arabia PIF have put 25 per cent of Newcastle United up for sale.

The exclusive comes from David Ornstein and Chris Waugh at The Athletic.

They reveal that this would be done through the issuing of new shares.

The Athletic stating: ‘The proposed transaction would see new investors inject funds directly into the club, receiving up to a quarter shareholding in exchange. No funds would flow to PIF, but its existing stake would be diluted by the share issue.’

They add that JP Morgan (the New York City-headquartered global bank) has been appointed advisors and that the process to find investment is under way.

The Athletic journalists detailing: ‘Sources with knowledge of the situation, speaking on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to do so publicly, insisted that, at this point, a minority investor is being sought with PIF eager to raise money, in part to fund major infrastructure projects, and regard the issuing of new shares as a good means of doing so.’

It appears that the 25 per cent of the total shareholding to be sold will come from the 84 per cent of the club owned by the Saudi Arabia PIF, as the report adds that: ‘The British Reuben family owns the remaining 16 per cent shareholding and Jamie Reuben is their representative on the board.’

Back in May 2026, The Athletic had previously reported that the Newcastle United majority owners were open to selling a minority stake to help fund significant infrastructure projects: ‘However, people familiar with the matter insisted PIF retained a long-term commitment to the club they jointly bought from Mike Ashley for a total of £305million ($400.1m at present exchange rates) in 2021, though they were willing to dilute their shareholding and had already been approached by possible investors. Yasir Al-Rumayyan, PIF’s governor and Newcastle’s chairman, attended his first match of the season at St James’ Park on Saturday, watching Newcastle draw 2-2 with league champions Arsenal. Jamie Reuben was also at the match.’

This news today hopefully signals a new stadium will go ahead, as well as the state of the art training ground.

The Athletic adding: ‘While PIF was never going to pay for a new stadium outright — Newcastle have always been viewed as a long-term investment intended to bring them an eventual profit — any project of that scale would require a notable injection of equity as well as outside financing.’

#1934. Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund Prediction, Odds, H2H and Betting Tips

Ryan Fletcher is a lifelong GTA fan who runs Read GTA. He's played the series since GTA III came out, followed by Vice City and San Andreas, which he still plays to this day. He's most interested in the technical side of the games and he built the platform Read GTA runs on.

The leaders of the Premier League against the leaders of the Bundesliga, under the lights at the Emirates. That’s the kind of Champions League night we waited years for, and now it’s a regular Tuesday. The champions are six points clear at home, unbeaten in Europe and up against a Dortmund side that hasn’t lost a league game all season.

There’s a twist, though. David Raya is out, so Kepa gets the gloves, and Saturday’s 2-2 at St James’ Park showed that this team can still be got at. This Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund preview covers everything you need before the 8pm kick-off. That means the latest odds, team news for both sides, predicted line-ups, the head-to-head record, the key stats and our prediction and betting tips.

The bookies make Arsenal strong favourites, as you’d expect with this home record in Europe. Dortmund are big outsiders for a side that’s top of the Bundesliga, and that tells you how highly the market rates the Gunners at the Emirates. Prices were checked on matchday and will move once the team sheets are out, so always check before you bet.

Those prices make Arsenal roughly a 67% chance, with the draw around 19% and Dortmund around 14% once the bookmaker margin is stripped out.

Be careful with the scorer lists, because some bookmakers still have Martin Zubimendi priced up and he’s injured.

The big news is in goal. Raya came off with a shoulder problem at Newcastle and Arteta confirmed he won’t be fit for tonight, though he said it “doesn’t look too serious” and surgery isn’t needed. Kepa Arrizabalaga steps in.

Missing Saka is a blow, but Madueke has stepped up brilliantly. He rescued a point at Newcastle and Arteta called him “decisive” in his press conference. Zubimendi’s absence means Myles Lewis-Skelly is the most likely option to partner Declan Rice in midfield.

Kepa; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapié; Lewis-Skelly, Rice; Madueke, Ødegaard, Eze; Gyökeres.

Saliba being back is a big boost, and there’s a real chance he comes straight in. Havertz is also pushing for a start up front.

Dortmund had two big worries going into this one, and both look like they’ve cleared. Kovač said Serhou Guirassy and Carney Chukwuemeka trained on Monday and are “ready for tomorrow’s match”. Guirassy missed the weekend win at Gladbach with a hamstring problem, so whether he’s fit enough to start is still a question.

Our very own Ethan Nwaneri is on loan at Dortmund and is allowed to play against us. He hasn’t started a game since mid-October, so expect him on the bench. It would be very Arsenal for him to come off it and score, so let’s hope not.

Kobel; Anton, Schlotterbeck, Bensebaini; Ryerson, Nmecha, Bellingham, Svensson; Beier, Karetsas; Silva.

If Guirassy is fit to start, he comes in for Silva. He’s scored four goals in four Champions League games this season, so he’s the man to watch.

Arsenal and Dortmund have met eight times in competitive football, all in the Champions League group stage. Arsenal have won four, Dortmund three, and one has been a draw.

Don’t read too much into the friendly in August. It’s the competitive record that counts, and Dortmund have won just once in their last eight trips to England.

Arsenal have scored eight and conceded only three in Europe this season, with three of their four games away from home. Dortmund have scored seven and conceded five, and they haven’t kept a clean sheet in the Champions League yet.

Arsenal are top of the Premier League on 28 points from 11 games, six clear of Brighton. Saturday’s draw at Newcastle ended a five-match winning run in the league. Eze put us ahead, Newcastle turned it around after the break, and Madueke got us out of jail.

Dortmund are unbeaten in ten Bundesliga games and sit two points clear of Bayern. They’ve conceded only seven league goals, the fewest in Germany, and Felix Nmecha’s goal at Gladbach on Saturday took them back above Bayern. They also showed a bit of fight by drawing late at Bayern in October, although they let a 2-0 lead slip at home to Werder Bremen.

Four straight clean sheets at home in the Champions League is serious form. But Dortmund nearly always score, and with Kepa in goal instead of Raya there’s a bit more risk. The safer way to back an Arsenal win is to pair it with under 3.5 goals rather than paying 4/11 for a straight win. The 2-0 at 11/2 is a decent shout for anyone wanting a bigger price.

He’s the most likely scorer on the night, and Dortmund’s back line hasn’t kept a clean sheet in Europe all season. For those who like the shots markets, Gyökeres to have two or more shots on target at 8/5 is worth a look too.

This is a closer call than it looks. Dortmund score in nearly every game, but Arsenal haven’t conceded in four home games in Europe. If Saliba comes back in, BTTS no at odds-against becomes even more attractive.

Arsenal to win, under 3.5 goals and Gyökeres to score. That fits a 2-0 or 2-1 win, which is exactly the kind of result we’d expect.

Arsenal at 4/11 isn’t much of a price as a single, so plenty of Gooners will be tying the win into a bigger slip. This is a two-night matchday, with more games tomorrow, so there’s plenty to choose from. If you want ideas for the rest of the round, the football accumulators site lists acca picks for both nights of Champions League action, sorted by market and price. You’ll find selections across match result, double chance, both teams to score, goals lines and scorer markets. Prices are checked every two hours, there’s a public results log, and it doesn’t take bets itself, so you still pick your own bookmaker. The picks come from bookmaker prices and not from the team news, so do your own checks, especially on a night when Raya is out.

Our advice is to keep your acca short. Arsenal look a safe enough leg, but adding too many short-priced selections can turn a good bet into a bad one.

Dortmund are a good side and they’ll fancy their chances with Guirassy back. Their press could make life uncomfortable for Kepa early on. But Arsenal are unbeaten in 19 Champions League games and haven’t conceded in four home games in Europe, and Dortmund’s away record in England is poor.

We expect Arsenal to be patient, dominate the ball and grind out a win that puts us right in the mix for a top-two finish in the league phase. Madueke and Gyökeres look the most likely men to make the difference.

Arsenal are around 4/11 to win, the draw is about 4/1 and Dortmund are around 13/2 to 7/1.

No. Raya is out with a shoulder injury, so Kepa Arrizabalaga will start in goal.

#1933. Kepa handed Arsenal opportunity to prove he can fill Raya’s boots against Dortmund

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

With David Raya out, Kepa Arrizabalaga has a great chance to prove that he is more than just an Arsenal cup keeper. Mikel Arteta needs to have confidence in his number two. He needs to ensure that he upholds the same high bar set by the starting keeper as Borussia Dortmund come to the Emirates.

Raya has been ruled out of tonight’s Champions League game following a shoulder problem which he picked up in Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle United.

Whilst the initial diagnosis is good news, surgery is not required. Further tests will determine Raya’s recovery period.

As previously mentioned, Kepa will be stepping in for Raya at St James’ Park. Moreover, Arteta has stated his preferred choice of player in this situation. It seems that Illan Meslier will miss out on the opportunity to play this time.

As well as playing for Arsenal, the Spaniard has formerly played in the Champions League for Chelsea and Real Madrid. He has already appeared 14 times for the Gunners. Including in the league stage match which saw them beat Kairat Almaty.

Whilst Kepa has typically been second choice to Raya, his game time has mostly been in the EFL Cup. He will now need to prove himself as a trustworthy option for Arsenal should Raya be injured or otherwise unable to play.

As well as being a good goalkeeper, Raya is also good at passing and positioning. This in turn assists Arsenal in attacking from the back line.

Ex-Arsenal midfielder Paul Merson has acknowledged the quality that Spanish goalkeepers have at creating good defensive and central positioning. This can frequently be an under-recognised yet important component in Arsenal’s build-up play.

Like Arsenal, Kepa will also have to remain calm when playing out from the back. Although Kepa does not necessarily need to replicate all of Raya’s qualities, he will need to have good decision-making skills as well as good communication.

Meslier is still in contention, having played in the Carabao Cup game against Fleetwood Town. Kepa has been Arsenal’s number two keeper in the Premier League and was able to rush on in for Raya when he was substituted at Newcastle.

It does seem that Kepa is the obvious option, and he can further cement his position in Arteta’s team.

Arsenal’s schedule is demanding. They are playing Manchester City on a Sunday and there are also worries about Raya’s fitness. So far, the club has not yet received medical information on Raya’s status.

Then there is Dortmund. They have already secured victories in their first four games in the Champions League and are level on points with Arsenal in the league section.

Kepa does not have a great deal of flexibility. Arsenal require the new goalkeeper to offer them security.

In case Raya needs more time to recover, it is necessary for Arteta to be able to guarantee that there is an effective replacement.

For Kepa, it is equally an opportunity to prove that he can assume this leadership position for the team during important moments.

#1932. Aston Villa and Newcastle United restricting competition parallels are now impossible to ignore

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Aston Villa and Newcastle United, two clubs with plenty in common.

Newcastle United winning a first major trophy in decades in 2025.

Aston Villa winning a first major trophy in decades in 2026.

In recent years Newcastle United getting into the Champions League not once, but twice, for the first time in decades.

In recent years Aston Villa getting into the Champions League not once, but twice, for the first time in decades (since the days it was called the European Cup).

The two clubs with proud histories also have another far bigger thing in common.

They are by far and away the two disruptor Premier League clubs, the pair who have tried hardest to break the modern day ‘Big Six’ financial stranglehold on long-term power and success.

Aston Villa and Newcastle United have flown closest to the Sun and suffered because of it, with UEFA SCR restrictions battering them into submission. If you don’t follow their warnings and get back in financial check, then face a ban from the Champions League (and other UEFA competitions) in the future.

It is all part of the endless vicious circle for clubs such as Aston Villa and Newcastle United who are attempting to narrow that yawning financial chasm that exists between themselves and the ‘Premier League Big Six’ who have been allowed to build such seemingly unchallengeable financial powerhouses across many years when Mike Ashley ran United into the ground and Villa suffered in many ways of their own.

This is the Champions League story of recent years for Aston Villa and Newcastle United.

2022-23 season Newcastle United qualify for next season’s Champions League but Aston Villa don’t.

2023-24 season Newcastle United compete in that season’s Champions League but Aston Villa don’t. Aston Villa qualify for next season’s Champions League but Newcastle United don’t.

2024-25 season Aston Villa compete in that season’s Champions League but Newcastle United don’t. Newcastle United qualify for next season’s Champions League but Aston Villa don’t.

2025-26 season Newcastle United compete in that season’s Champions League but Aston Villa don’t. Aston Villa qualify for next season’s Champions League but Newcastle United don’t.

2026-27 season Aston Villa compete in that season’s Champions League but Newcastle United don’t. Qualifying for…Aston Villa??? Newcastle United???

2026-27 season Competing/Qualifying for…Aston Villa??? Newcastle United???

The pattern couldn’t be clearer for Aston Villa and Newcastle United in recent years.

An ability every other year to qualify for the Champions League BUT in years when playing in the top European competition, unable to also qualify for the following season’s Champions League.

Four seasons in a row we have had either Newcastle United or Aston Villa disrupting the route of Premier League Big Six clubs to the Champions League BUT from where I am standing, it looks like that run is going to end now. I find it very unlikely that either Aston Villa or Newcastle United will qualify via the Premier League.

I think that now things have well and truly caught up with the two clubs and their ambitions.

I think to properly stand a chance of having a season where you can compete in the Champions League and attempt to qualify via the Premier League for the following season’s UCL competition, you need to have a squad with enough quality and depth to cope.

The financial rules make this all but impossible for Aston Villa and Newcastle United as things stand.

Wages are the most crippling thing, the Premier League Big Six are able to pay far bigger wages than Newcastle United and Aston Villa. It reaches a point where they can’t pay their star plays anything close to the market rate (what they can get elsewhere). It also means that to try and somehow have a large enough squad to cope with both Premier League and Champions League, you need to sells some/all of your best players so you can afford to bring in enough signings to try and give you the depth.

The reality in recent years when Aston Villa and Newcastle United have been trying to do both, compete in the Champions League AND qualify for next season’s, they have to play their small group of very best players far too often. This all but guarantees these star players will pick up injuries and/or get fatigued and their effectiveness is vastly diminished.

I think the perfect storm has now arrived.

All of the above issues have been impacted by the Premier League PSR and now SCR restrictions BUT even more so by the far stricter UEFA SCR restrictions on allowed spending on transfer fees and wages as a proportion of your revenues (UEFA allows 70% of ‘Adjusted operating revenue’).

I know that as football fans (especially those of Newcastle United and Aston Villa) we are heartily sick of all the accountancy boring side of things and how it constantly impacts the coverage of Premier League clubs these days.

To simply spell it out though, it basically means that if your revenues are twice as big as another club’s, you can spend twice as much on wages and transfer fees.

Roughly speaking, the likes of Arsenal, Liverpool, Man City and Man U have twice as big revenues as Aston Villa and Newcastle United have per season, whilst Chelsea and Tottenham are also way ahead AND have various other elements that give them an inbuilt advantage, which has been put in place across many years.

This past summer transfer window, in order to comply with UEFA SCR restrictions and avoid a future ban on taking part in UEFA competitions, both Villa and Newcastle had to take drastic action when it came to buying and selling players AND their wage bills.

It would have been unrealistic and reckless this summer for a club like Villa or Newcastle to agree to long-term huge wages of a level that ‘Big Six’ clubs can comfortably afford.

You then have Newcastle United and Aston Villa also having to sell at least some of their best players because they generally bring in the biggest instant benefit to a club’s accounts. The transfer fee agreed (less the player’s current book value) all goes into that current season’s accounts as a profit. However, when a player is bought the transfer fee that is agreed is spread over the length of his contract, when it comes to showing as a cost in the annual accounts. So if you sign a player for £50m on a five year contract, each season it shows as a £10m cost in the accounts. So basically if you sell a player for a big transfer fee it can help you afford a number of players for a total higher than that transfer fee BUT they still eventually have to be accounted for. Plus of course all Premier League clubs are constantly having those annual transfer fee costs for previous signings going into the accounts.

So what did Aston Villa and Newcastle United do in summer 2026?

They both sold a lot of their best and highest paid players to other clubs. In general, these players went to clubs who paid them far higher wages. Then Villa and Newcastle generally recruited players on lower transfer fees, many of who they also hope will improve in terms of value as well as ability in years to come.

Newcastle United lost the likes of Gordon, Trippier, Bruno and Tonali, having previously had to sell Isak and sacrifice Minteh and Anderson as well.

As well as previous players they had been forced to trade, this summer Aston Villa moved on the likes of Rogers, Watkins, Martinez, Digne, Konsa and Tielemans.

Interesting to see where many of these players are now at:

Bruno (Arsenal), Rogers (Chelsea), Isak (Liverpool), Tielemans (Man U), Tonali (Tottenham), Martinez (Chelsea), Anderson (Man City), Konsa (Arsenal)…

So not only are Aston Villa and Newcastle United forced to move on many of their best players in order to stay inside the UEFA and EPL SCR restrictions, they then see most of them end up at the very Premier League Big Six clubs that they are trying to compete with, against the odds.

When it comes to power and success long-term, it feels very much like tossing a coin and it is heads the Premier League Big Six win, whilst tails sees Villa and Newcastle lose.

Aston Villa and Newcastle United currently sit 12th and 13th in the Premier League table, from 11 attempts each they have won three EPL matches apiece.

Where might the pair have been instead if the financial restrictions didn’t leave them hamstrung?

What if they weren’t prevented from matching the wages that Premier League Big Six clubs are able to pay, were able to keep all of their best players AND bring in similar quality ones that would help persuade them to stay AND enable them to properly compete long-term?

#1931. Two players under huge scrutiny – for very different reasons | Portsmouth v West Ham United

Scott Parker withdrawing goal keeper Mads Hermansen from the firing line for a bit of breather has resonated well with West Ham supporters, who were all very much in favour of replacing him after a dreadful run of form. The statistics were pretty damning with the Dane unable to lay a glove on any one of the last dozen goals hit past him.

Herrick can cement his place with a decent performance at Fratton Park tonight

Herrick needs a clean sheet in the next couple of games to cement his place in the side and his confidence, after a cock up led to Preston’s goal at the weekend: All eyes will be on him come the first corner at Fratton Park tonight to see how he shapes up.

Portsmouth, however, have their own goal keeping problems and their very own Mads Hermansen in the shape of stopper Nicholas Schmid who has made his own string of errors in recent games, leading to a fairly frank rating last time out from Portsmouth.co.uk:

“Nicolas Schmid – 4: Poor mistake gifted Bolton an equaliser just five minutes after Blues took the lead. While a poor kick out of his hands almost proved costly too. That’s five goal-cost mistakes in six games now. Hugely worrying.”

Pompey’s boss John Mousinho has publicly backed his 29 year old Austrian, which means he’s likely to start against West Ham tonight and the message for Scott Parker’s team is 100% crystal clear.

Test the keeper. Again and again. And follow up on those shots. Sounds simple. West Ham however haven’t exactly found it easy to hit the target with 26 wayward efforts against Preston.

Either way there’ll be huge scrutiny on both the men between the sticks tonight.

Portsmouth v West Ham United, Fratton Park, kick off 7.45 pm.

‘Player ratings’ on Claret and Hugh after the final whistle.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

It is half time . Thought it couldn’t get any worse. Parkers selection has been shown go be awful. Herrick is not close to being ready and AGAIN Kilman is abysmal. If Parker can’t see it he shouldn’t be managing anything above 3rd division . Abysmal performance to match the abysmal selections.

Hermansen simply isn’t good enough. We desperately need to sign a top keeper and centre forward

Hope Herrick stays. In fact would keep the same backline even though want to see Golambeckis + Dinos selected sometime. Thought Morato had a very average match, a bit slow to react, but he too deserves a chance as only his 1st game at CB. Veltman combined well with Bowen.

It is in midfield I am wondering what the team will be. Keep Alvarez who played well, but just as importantly, kept a level head which we need with so many youngsters in the team. In fact a 4-man midfield is a selection any WHU manager could easily make, because we have so much quality in midfield and they each bring different qualities to a team. Mukasa/Kante for example. Both still learning, but very good and what a contrast.

Desperately want Kante in the team, will Orford make an entrance?, …

Whoever our keeper is, Parker needs to protect them and keep Kilman out of the side

The Stats dont lie, less clean sheets last season when Kilman played, and certainly not mamy this seadon either

Herrick didn’t do badly, he deserves another shot.

I’ll be happy just to break the Groundhog Day of going behind and chasing games, surely we’ve seen enough of that now….

#1930. Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

So much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

They can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

City will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s

There is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a new City, different personnel and even a new look.

They wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

The Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

“I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a new team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw

Phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are new to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

Bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

“In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca said. “This shows how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”

By Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he showed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

City had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

“It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland said. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the big stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”

For Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS

Man City have now won seven of their last eight opening matchdays in the UEFA Champions League 🔵Starting strong 💪 pic.twitter.com/CIjsMj4Dig

“I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. It is a special competition and all the games are very difficult. He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] never panicked and was very good. The performance from him was unbelievable. I am happy to reunite with Enzo [Fernandez], who was very good.”

36 - Erling Haaland scored his 36th UEFA Champions League goal for Manchester City, equalling Sergio Agüero as joint-most for the Citizens in the competition.Inevitability. pic.twitter.com/HHbNadybxh

“I am so happy with how my teammates have welcomed me into the club. They are not just great players but great human beings. The fans have been absolutely brilliant and this is a new step in my career. Erling [Haaland] is an animal, a beast. Every time I am on the pitch, I will look for him and look to assist him. He is an amazing human being and helped me settle in. I am happy Enzo [Maresca] did all he good to make the move happen. I am so grateful for everything he has done for me and my family.”

5️⃣9️⃣ appearances 5️⃣9️⃣ goals@Erling's #UCL record 🤯 pic.twitter.com/v6IvpwC9vm

“Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a tough game, they play amazing football. We had to deliver on the biggest stage and we did. We controlled the whole of the first half. We created a lot of chances. They pushed us for a good 25 minutes in the second half but we pulled through. These are the games we have to win. We have had a great start to the season.

“He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] had a really good game and he has been amazing in training. I think we have a gem there. We have to learn and Enzo [Maresca] demands a lot from us. We demand a lot from each other. It was an unreal atmosphere so I hope Enzo is happy with that.”

AEK Athens 1 LASK 0 Club Brugge 2 Aston Villa 3 Dortmund 3 Villarreal 2 Lille 2 Real Betis 3 Porto 0 Manchester City 2 Real Madrid 2 Inter Milan 1

The final whistle is blown and Manchester City begin their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 win in Porto. Erling Haaland’s double gives Enzo Maresca a victory in his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City.

Enzo has two shots from range in quick succession, one from a free-kick. The free-kick goes just wide and the second is saved by D Costa.

It has been an ill-tempered game and tempers have boiled over again. Rosario and Haaland are involved in a tussle on the floor, which then leads to a mass melee. Haaland and Rosario are both booked for their part in starting that. Haaland is pleased that he got booked but I am not sure why. Both played their part in that melee.

Enzo Maresca’s side will head home with all three points. Ait-Nouri’s cross from the left side of the box picks out Haaland, who first-time shot from 10 yards out picks out the far corner. A clinical finish from Haaland and Manchester City will start their Champions League campaign with a win.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw

That is really poor refereeing. Porto are denied two clear fouls before Rosario is then punished for a foul on Enzo, which was a foul but so too were the previous two incidents. Francesco Farioli is then booked for his protestations but you can understand their frustration.

Ait-Nouri has the chance to warp up the three points with an effort from the edge of the box but his shot with his weaker right foot goes narrowly wide.

Nothing comes from the corner as Hwang’s delivery to the front post is dreadful.

Haaland has his fourth headed chance of the game but this one goes over the bar from Ndiaye’s cross. Haaland has scored one of those chances but spurned some good ones.

Down the other end, Fofana, only just on, wins Porto a corner and whips up the home fans.

A final change of the night for Porto sees Fofana replace Veiga. One last roll of the dice from Francisco Farioli.

Whilst Manchester City’s lead is only 1-0, Porto will believe an equaliser is there for them. However, the momentum they were building 10/15 minutes ago has seemingly been lost and the visitors have managed to wrestle back a bit more control.

That is a big chance missed by Pepe. Gimenez receives it down the left and pings a cross to the back post. The cross perfectly picks out Pepe, who fluffs his lines and completely mis-kicks.

Manchester City are making their final two substitutions of the night as Kovacic and Ait-Nouri come on for Bouaddi and Foden. Ait-Nouri looks like he is going to play left wing.

Two more changes for Porto as Silva and M Fernandes are replaced by Gimenez and Moura.

Porto are going to make their first two changes of the night as Hwang and former Norwich man Sainz come on. Varela and Gomes head off.

For the second time in the half, Donnarumma is lucky. To be fair to the Manchester City keeper, the pass back to him is poor but he is then fortunate. His attempted ball out to his left is intercepted by Gomes but it rolls behind for a goal kick. That ball could have rolled straight into the Manchester City net or fallen straight back at Gomes feet with an empty net ahead of him. Donnarumma was very lucky on Saturday against Coventry to avoid a calamitous moment and he is lucky to avoid another awful moment for the second time in quick succession.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn

Ndiaye receives it out on the left before driving inside. He gets his shot away from the edge of the box and tries to pick out the far corner but it is too close to D Costa and an easy save for the Porto keeper.

A fine pass from Rosario inside his own half cuts through Manchester City’s midfield sends Varela racing through the Manchester City half. He plays it out to his right to find Gomes, who cuts inside onto his left before trying to beat Donnarumma at his near post but the shot goes wide.

Enzo Maresca responds to a shift in momentum in this game making a double change. Anderson and Ndiaye come on for Cherki and Semenyo.

Porto have started to gain some momentum and they want a penalty. Bouaddi is perhaps a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul right on the edge of the box but it may have been just outside the penalty area. You can feel the game starting to turn in Porto’s favour.

Varela is inches away from an equaliser for Porto and plenty of the home fans thought the ball was in the net. Varela sends a curling effort towards goal from the edge of the box but it goes narrowly wide.

That was a glorious chance for Porto to equalise. A corner is sent in from the left to the back post, where Alberto heads it back across goal. However, none of his teammates, including Silva, could tap the ball into the net. Porto should probably be back on level terms.

Donnrumma is a very, very lucky man. Porto would have had a certain penalty as Donnarumma completely flattened Pepe but the latter was offside so it is no penalty. Donnarumma has been booked but avoids a penalty, which would have been a guarantee had Pepe been onside.

Just three minutes into the second half, Enzo Maresca has made a substitution. Gvardiol, on a yellow, is withdrawn and Khusanov is brought on.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was embracing Daniel Sturridge in the press box and they weren’t in their seats when the goal went in. Lovely move from City and Haaland steered in his 58th goal in the competition.

Erling Haaland moves 7th in the ALL-TIME UCL top-scorers list 💪🇳🇴📊 pic.twitter.com/oIkrPxm0gT

Haaland wasted two headed opportunities in the first half but he does not spurn this chance. It is a first Manchester City assist for Enzo, who clips in a cross from the left side of the box. Haaland meets it and his header glances off the far post and goes in.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s

Gabriel Clarke on Amazon Prime has reported that there was some trouble in the tunnel as the two sides went off for half-time. Both sets of security teams for the clubs were forced to step in.

We are back under way in Porto. Tempers were really starting to boil over as that first half wore on so will that continue into the second half?

The former Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea striker has described the incident involving Marc Guehi and Gabri Veiga as a “nasty collision” and “it does not look good at all”. I think Guehi is a lucky man to still be on the pitch as some VAR officials would surely have recommended a review for that foul. Porto boss Francesco Farioli felt Guehi led with his elbow and the home fans were not happy with that as well as a number of other decisions in that first half.

Marc Guehi absolutely clattered Gabri Veiga 🤯🤕 pic.twitter.com/Fh5ippv3cK
