#1848. Erling Haaland sees Man City equaliser DISALLOWED in controversial circumstances - with fans and pundits split over whether Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno had both hands on the ball after fumbled strike

By HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER

Published: 08:35 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 11:06 EST, 21 November 2026

Erling Haaland saw a first half equaliser controversially disallowed against Fulham, as Enzo Maresca's side only managed to fight back to earn a disappointing draw.

Haaland latched onto a beautifully bent cross from Iliman Ndiaye to bundle home from less than eight minutes after Rodrigo Muniz had given the visitors a shock lead at the Etihad.

But despite Bernd Leno appearing to fumble the ball over the line and the referee's watch flashing to signify a goal, the man in the middle ruled the equaliser out for a foul on the Cottagers goalkeeper.

The decision has left both fans and pundits torn over whether the decision was harsh or whether it was the right call.

Former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Karen Carney said her mind changed after having watched a replay of the incident.

Speaking on TNT Sports from the Etihad, she said: 'My initial reaction was I thought the goalkeeper didn’t have control of it, and it should've been a goal, but then when you slow it down, (you can see it).

Erling Haaland has the ball in the back of the net, but it’s ruled out! ❌ 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/sKqY8Q7a9Z

Erling Haaland has a first half equaliser for Man City chalked off against Fulham

'People are going to shout at me through the TV. But I think the referee made the right decision.'

Tottenham legend Glenn Hoddle, also on punditry duty in Manchester, felt the same.

He said: 'I don’t know whether he had control of it, but I don’t think that comes into it. I think that’s the right decision, but it’s a very tough call. It could have gone either way.'

The Premier League Match Centre clarified why the decision was made by Tom Bramall and the VAR team in Stockley Park.

A statement on social media read: 'The referee’s call of free-kick to Fulham and no goal to Manchester City was checked and confirmed by VAR – with the goalkeeper deemed to be in control of the ball.'

They added that the VAR said: 'The ball is in control between both hands and then is played out of that possession by the attacker, and then into the back of the net.'

The laws of the game state that a goalkeeper is believed to be in control of the ball when the ball is 'between their hands/arms or between their hand(s)/arm(s) and any surface'.

Not all fans, of a Manchester City persuasion or not, felt that the right decision was made. Some believed that both Haaland and City should feel hard done by.

Haaland was left in disbelief by the referee's decision with many fans feeling the same

An Arsenal fan made their stance clear: 'Even as a rival, I honestly think this Haaland goal should’ve stood for Manchester City. Would’ve been p***** off if a Gyokeres goal like this for Arsenal was cancelled.'

A different fan added: 'Manchester City has been robbed. Haaland scored a clean goal here. The ball went in even before Haaland had contact with the keeper.

Not everyone agreed, though, with many X users taking the opposite stance.

One said: 'It’s explicitly a foul under the Laws. Don’t blame the ref if you don’t like the laws.'

Another user wrote: 'I am also an Arsenal fan but the ball is still in two-palm contact. If you allow it, you will encourage outfield player challenging the save attempt And a foot to hand challenge will much more often lead to a broken wrist or thumb. That is an unfair advantage to outfield players.'

City did go on to equalise in the second half, with Elliot Anderson bagging his first Premier League goal for the club by smashing home a sublime volley in the 57th minute.

#1846. I watched Rangers edge five-goal thriller vs Aberdeen and noted a title-winning trait and blossoming talent

Rangers produced a quickfire second-half comeback to beat Aberdeen 3-2 at Ibrox and move to within a point of Scottish Premiership leaders Celtic on Tuesday night.

After trailing to Brad Lyons' first-half header, which was deemed to have crossed the line by VAR despite Nico Raskin’s attempt to clear the ball, the hosts struck three times in a blistering spell after the interval through Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Raskin.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Findlay Marshall's immediate reply ensured a tense finale, but Rangers held on to secure a vital three points and extend their unbeaten run to 14 matches. Derek McInnes’ side now have the chance to move top of the table on Saturday when they host high-flying Falkirk.

Lewis Anderson watched the action unfold for The Scotsman and picks out his three main takeaways from an absorbing five-goal thriller.

Once again, Rangers found a way to win. Their impressive run of results in recent months has been built on an increasingly familiar trait: an ability to secure three points even when performances fall short of the required standard. Against an enterprising Aberdeen outfit, however, McInnes' men were given a proper examination before eventually claiming another victory.

McInnes' decision to started with a back three, with Ben Godfrey drafted into the starting line-up for the first time since late July, raised eyebrows and ultimately failed to provide the defensive solidity he would have hoped for. The Dons repeatedly found opportunities to exploit the space around Rangers' exposed backline, particularly during a first half in which the visitors looked the more purposeful side.

Aberdeen played with an intensity that unsettled the hosts. Rangers’ combinations lacked precision, their wide players failed to make a sufficient impact and their build-up play was too laboured to trouble their opponents consistently.

McInnes’ response was decisive, with Kim Min-Su, Findlay Curtis and Tuur Rommens introduced at half-time. It signalled an acknowledgement that significant changes were required. Rangers emerged with greater urgency and attacking intent, and Naderi's equaliser provided the spark for a thrilling turnaround.

For a spell, Rangers looked capable of putting the contest beyond doubt, taking full advantage of the momentum generated by their early second-half goals. Yet just as they appeared to have wrestled the match under control, another defensive lapse allowed Aberdeen to threaten a comeback.

The victory was never entirely comfortable, nor was the performance perfect. But Rangers' capacity to respond to adversity and find a way remains an increasingly valuable asset. They continue to collect the points needed to maintain their title challenge and now have the opportunity to move to the top of the Premiership before Celtic take to the pitch this weekend.

Aberdeen will return north frustrated by the outcome, but newly-appointed head coach Mario Frick can take considerable encouragement from a performance which offered a glimpse of what his side might become under his stewardship.

For long periods, the visitors carried a genuine threat on the counter-attack and had sufficient opportunities to leave Ibrox with something to show for their efforts. Their defensive collapse during Rangers' devastating burst after half-time proved costly, with goalkeeper Marius Muller's handling error providing the catalyst for the hosts' revival.

Yet Aberdeen's response was equally striking. Having been left shell-shocked, they gathered themselves and went after Rangers with renewed conviction, refusing to accept that the contest had slipped beyond them. Findlay Marshall's goal, an impressive contribution from a player still only 20, gave them fresh belief and brought the prospect of an unlikely recovery tantalisingly close.

There was a vibrancy about this Aberdeen display which has been conspicuously absent for much of their recent past under Stephen Robinson. They played with ambition, conviction and a willingness to commit bodies forward, while their response to adversity suggested a resilience which Frick will be keen to nurture.

Aside from the damaging 12-minute spell in which Rangers scored three times, the visitors showed plenty of grounds for optimism. Their organisation was better, their pressing purposeful and their attacking play carried a level of intent which repeatedly troubled the hosts’ rear-guard.

The result will sting, not least because they had done enough in spells to believe a point was within their grasp. But there was little about this performance to suggest Frick intends to oversee a cautious rebuilding exercise. If anything, Aberdeen look set to embrace a more adventurous identity, which should please supporters.

Aberdeen have a seriously talented prospect on their hands in 20-year-old Findlay Marshall, who was influential throughout. The midfielder won the corner which led to Lyons' opener before scoring a sublime second-half goal after being picked out by Alexander Briedl, which set up a tense finale.

His energy and attacking intent made him one of Aberdeen's most dangerous players and offered Frick further evidence of the his undoubted potential. Marshall displayed a maturity and composure which belied his age, combining an impressive work rate with an eye for goal. In defeat, he emerged with considerable credit.

The Rangers No.1’s contribution was arguably as important as the three goals at the opposite end. His first-half fingertip save from Ayoub Mouloua prevented Aberdeen establishing a two-goal advantage. The Croatian’s work was not finished there. After the interval, he made a fine stop at his near post to thwart Nicky Devlin before denying Marshall as Aberdeen searched for an equaliser.

Rangers' second-half attacking burst will dominate the headlines, but without Pandur's crucial interventions the outcome could have been very different.

#1844. Rangers’ knack for winning ugly is becoming a habit but utility man wants fewer self-inflicted scares

James Penrice believes Rangers are acquiring the habit of winning ugly and grinding out results as their Premiership title challenge gathers momentum, but has warned they must address their tendency to surrender control after taking commanding positions in matches.

A gritty 3-2 victory over Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday night brought Rangers to within a point of Celtic at the Premiership summit and extended their unbeaten sequence to 14 games. It was also another test of their resilience, with a disjointed first-half display giving way to an emphatic response after the interval, when Rangers struck three times in a blistering 12-minute spell.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The hosts had gone in at half-time trailing to Brad Lyons’ header, prompting McInnes to make a triple substitution and reshape his side. The changes had an immediate impact, with Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Nico Raskin all finding the net during a devastating spell early in the second half. However, Findlay Marshall’s reply ensured Rangers were unable to enjoy a comfortable conclusion to the match.

Penrice, who operated in a midfield three alongside Raskin and Dan Neil, praised the character shown by his team-mates to secure another welcome three points, but was equally candid about the frailties which threatened to undermine the victory.

“Very mixed, I think,” he said when asked for his assessment of an absorbing contest. “We conceded in the first half, but came flying out of the traps after the break. I thought we were really good for 10 or 15 minutes. We scored the third and looked comfortable, but then we switched off. We made it difficult for ourselves again, but the main thing is that we walk away with three points.”

McInnes used the interval to make tactical changes, with Penrice crediting the substitutes for injecting the energy and intensity needed to wrestle control of the contest from Aberdeen.

“We made a couple of changes. I thought the boys that came on were brilliant, that real spark and energy,” he added. “We started the second half really well, but ultimately we need to score more. We could have done that and made it really easy for ourselves, but then again we switch off and we make it difficult.

“Ultimately, it's not a bad trait to be scoring late on sometimes and winning games, but as players we want to make it as easy as possible. Again, we’ve made it hard but we’re still winning games and going on a wee bit of a run now, so hopefully that continues.”

Penrice’s versatility has become an increasingly valuable asset for McInnes. Primarily a left-back, he has also been deployed in central and wide positions as the manager continues to adapt his tactical approach to suit each fixture.

“I'm not bothered where, I’ll play absolutely anywhere to help the team,” he admitted. “It’s a massive thing for me. We work on it [in training] but I've not really trained over the last couple of days, because I was feeling a wee strain so it was more just dealing with it. It's not alien to us, we've done it numerous times this season, guys playing in different positions.

“I've played in the middle, I've played out wide, so we should all be used to it now and we are. It just takes that adjustment period on the pitch but us as players we've got a responsibility when there's a plan in place and something's not going right we fix it ourselves. We don't need to go to the side and I think that's what the gaffer is looking for. He's looking for us to take responsibility on the pitch and we've got that now.”

Rangers have little time to dwell on their latest victory, with Falkirk due at Ibrox next on Saturday, a fixture that offers McInnes’ side the chance to leapfrog Celtic and move top of the Premiership table, having closed the gap on the leaders with their comeback win over Aberdeen.

“It's a massive incentive, but the league's not won in November,” Penrice declared. “It will be a difficult game. Falkirk are playing well and they've travelled well away from home. So we'll need to be on it. We can't go into the game on Saturday like we were tonight. We need to be better. We just need to concentrate on ourselves, it's another game to tick off, one at a time.”

#1842. AC Milan Women 3-2 Sassuolo: Grimshaw crucial after crazy first half

Christy Grimshaw was crucial as AC Milan Women finally got back to winning ways, following what was a rather crazy first half against Sassuolo.

After two defeats and a draw, dropping points in a silly fashion against Napoli last weekend, Milan Women needed to bounce back with a win today. Thankfully, that’s exactly what they managed to do, even if it wasn’t the most controlled performance.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Just looking at the scoreline and the timing of the goals is enough to understand the nature of the game. All five goals were scored in the first half and it doesn’t end there either. All five were scored within the first 27 minutes!

The veteran Grimshaw opened the scoring for the Rossonere after nine minutes, but Sassuolo found a way back into the game just two minutes later. The Scottish international decided to restore the lead just four minutes later, i.e. in the 15th minute.

Angelica Soffia then made things more comfortable with a third goal in the 24th minute, or at least so we thought. Just three minutes after that, Sassuolo scored again and thus brought some life into the game, even if Milan looked the better side.

Suzanne Bakker’s side actually dominated possession, had more shots on target and also had a higher xG, so the win definitely feels deserved. And boy was it needed! The situation in the standings is still not great, but at least they are now four points behind the Champions League zone.

#1841. Celtic make addition to Europa League squad after Mika Baur injury

Celtic have added Jota to their Europa League squad in place of the injured Mika Baur.

The Portuguese winger was initially left out as he fought his way back from a serious knee injury. But he could now feature in his homeland against Torreense on Thursday after continuing his comeback with a start in Saturday’s 4-1 win over St Mirren.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Baur was recently ruled out for up to 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage but manager Martin O’Neill had been waiting to see how the German international reacted once his protective boot was off.

Baur could miss the rest of the league stage though and O’Neill has acted before setting off for Portugal.

With Benjamin Nygren nursing a heel problem, O’Neill started with a midfield three of Callum McGregor, Luke McCowan and Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain on Saturday, while Oliver Sorensen is another option.

Meanwhile, O’Neill has challenged Celtic to complete their Europa League comeback after resurrecting hopes against Besiktas.

Celtic were heading for a fourth straight defeat and bottom spot when they went behind against the Turks but they were inspired by the introduction of Camilo Duran, Callum Osmand and Colby Donovan and sealed a 3-2 win.

They now face away games against Torreense and Omonia Nicosia as they bid to move up the table.

Looking back at their recent win, O’Neill told Celtic Player: “I thought it was terrific. Really terrific.

“Besiktas are a very fine football team. Very fine side. They were expecting to win and win handsomely. They’ve spent a lot of money. I think their wage bill is in excess of £100million. So from that aspect, it was a terrific win.

“The character of the side was really brilliant. Really, really brilliant to win so late, and to win in the fashion in which we did was terrific. So it gives us a little bit of a chance and we have to go and try to do something for these next two away games.

“If we make it through to the qualifying stages, it will be the first time any team has been beaten in their first three games and made it.

“So that in itself should be a target for us. The games are not easy, we know that. We need to win at least one of these two away games and we might even need four points to give us a chance in the last two matches.

“We have to take confidence from recent games and take that into the game on Thursday.”

Torreense sit 13th in the Portuguese second tier and will host Celtic 60 miles away from their home in Leiria, as their own stadium only has about 2,500 seats.

But they have already beaten Lillestrom and Ararat-Armenia in the Europa League and took the lead against Sunderland before the Premier League side netted a stoppage-time winner.

“They won the Portuguese Cup against Sporting Lisbon, which is some achievement,” O’Neill said. “I’ve been learning as much as I can about them and watching footage.”

#1840. Four first half goals for Hassocks in hammering of Hurst

Four first half goals away at Billingshurst showed Hassocks have not suffered any lasting damage from their midweek hammering in the Sussex Transport Senior Cup at the hands of Chichester City.

Chi relentlessly stuck six past the Robins on Tuesday night. Hassocks were equally unforgiving on Hurst, pocketing all three points before the half time whistle.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

No further goals were added nor needed after the break, allowing the Robins to take their foot of the pedal and James Westlake to rattle through the substitutions ahead of a huge upcoming five weeks which could be season-defining.

Hassocks go to Rusthall next Saturday for their first ever appearance in the third round of the FA Vase. A place in the last 32 of the national competition is up for grabs.

December then brings matches against Roffey, Guernsey, East Grinstead Town, Eastbourne United and Haywards Heath Town. Five games against teams in the top eight of the Southern Combination Premier Division all harbouring hopes of promotion.

"It's going to be busy, it's going to be hard," said James Westlake of those upcoming fixtures. "It is a tough run through until January time really. But those big games in the league are the ones we want to be competing in."

Billingshurst provided a different type of challenge. Several ingredients were there for a banana skin - a pitch already heavy before kick off, opposition fighting relegation and a popular former Robin in the home dugout.

Eddie French expressed his displeasure at the performance of the officials afterwards and it was hard not to have some sympathy for the ex-Hassocks favourite.

Certainly in relation to the bizarre series of decisions which saw the Robins awarded a penalty for their second goal of the afternoon, Nat Guest sent off and Billingshurst left to play for 70 minutes with 10 men.

Hassocks took the lead five minutes prior to that pivotal sequence of events. Playing down the hill, Omar Abdsami exchanged a one-two with Dan Perry to split open the centre of the Hurst defence.

Abdsami still needed to get around covering right back James Bendell. He did that via some quick feet before firing low and hard across Fraser Trigwell and into the far corner.

Trigwell provided another current link between the clubs whilst Hassocks introduced former Hurst midfielder Luke Brodie from their bench in the second half.

Then came the major talking point. Lewis Finney delivered a corner which Dan Turner met with a towering header. The ball was several feet over the line when it struck Guest in the hand.

Remarkably, the officials did not award the goal but instead gave the Robins a spot kick and sent Guest off for deliberate hand ball.

Chaos ensued with the surreal scenario of both Hassocks and Billingshurst players protesting against the same decision for different reasons.

Once order was restored, Finney put away the spot kick despite Trigwell diving the right way. And just to really rub salt into Hurst wounds, the initial corner Turner scored from was a clear goal kick too.

"I would certainly have been frustrated if that went against us with the awarding of the corner to start it all off," Westlake said afterwards.

"If you are a neutral watching the game, you would ask that the goal from Turner is given and it is not a sending off. It was a shame for them but I guess we already had a good foothold and would have been 2-0 up anyway."

Two very quickly became three and there was nothing controversial about the spectacular strike from Finney 120 seconds after his successful penalty.

Liam Hendy played a long ball forward which Perry won in the air. The flick dropped into the path of Finney, who hit a 25 yard dipping volley. Trigwell got a hand to it but could not keep it out.

Hassocks enjoyed near-total domination for the remainder of the first half with the Billingshurst X account posting at the interval: "To say this has been like the Alamo would be harsh on the Alamo as it has been more one-sided than that."

Tall striker Jamie Wilkes lent so far back that he was almost horizontal when putting a shot from a good position into orbit. Trigwell then made an excellent finger tip save diving low at his near post to keep out an Abdsami effort.

Having set up both Abdsami and Finney, Perry added the fourth himself five minutes before half time. Jack Troak started the move down the left and his square pass inside was beautifully back heeled to Finney by Darren Budd.

Finney glided past Jack Griffin and although Trigwell did well to parry away the shot, Perry followed up for a poacher's finish to open his Hassocks account.

Billingshurst will undoubtedly be happy to see the back of the Hitman. Five weeks ago he scored a hat-trick against them for East Grinstead Town with what turned out to be his final goals in a Wasps shirt.

French changed Hurst's shape for the second half and it allowed them to stem the flow of goals without ever really offering much going forward.

Ed Cooper did not have a serious save to make although Griffin and Kieran Britland both should have done better when shooting high and wide respectively.

Britland did at least have the excuse of losing his footing as he pulled the trigger. He was not the only one to slip and slide as the already challenging surface cut up massively the longer the game went on.

Chances at the other end for Hassocks came for Charlie Bonwick-Adams, who put a header straight at Trigwell. Finney guided a Troak cross wide of the front post and substitute Raging Joe Bull did everything right after overlapping Abdsami, receiving a pass and cutting inside only to shoot into an adjacent field.

Trigwell made an outstanding double save when pushing away a Budd piledriver from the edge of the box at full stretch before reacting quick enough to get up and deflect the follow up from Abdsami behind using his feet.

Turner hit a volley diverted behind by a fine block with the final opportunity of the game involving two more replacements. Lewis Croal headed down a cross for Big Alex Fair to shoot directly upwards rather than towards goal.

"We wanted to kick on in the second half but that obviously wasn't meant to be," Westlake added. "The lads have come off disappointed considering we couldn't score more goals. But a clean sheet, four goals and three points are the really important thing today."

Hassocks: Ed Cooper; Charlie Bonwick-Adams, Dan Turner, Liam Hendy, Jack Troak; Jamie Wilkes, Darren Budd; Devon Fender, Lewis Finney, Omar Abdsami, Dan Perry.

Subs: Liam Benson, Lewis Croal, Joe Bull, Luke Brodie, Alex Fair (used).

Starman: Lewis Finney converted a penalty for the second goal, scored a stunning volley for the third and set up Dan Perry for the fourth.

#1839. Mauricio Pochettino's Man United rallying cry: New boss promises fans it will be a 'SPECIAL' season - despite club sitting in drop zone - as he gets straight to work after flying from US

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER and LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 02:49 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 21 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino has issued a rallying cry to Manchester United supporters, promising that this is going to be a 'special season' despite their dismal start which sees them 18th in the Premier League with just one win from their opening 10 games.

The new Red Devils head coach landed in Manchester on Wednesday morning, hopping straight off a private jet to meet his new players, hours after leading the USA in his final game as their boss.

And during a busy first day among his new surroundings, the Argentine sent a direct message to the club's fanbase as he preached for unity.

'Hi Reds, here's it's Mauricio Pochettino,' he said via a video posted on United's X account at 7.15pm on Wednesday evening.

'I am looking forward to meeting you guys. I hear so many good things about you.

'I hope we bring all the happiness working together and connecting together.

A message from Mauricio 💬❤️🤳 #ShotOnSnapdragon pic.twitter.com/2lBLkMaGY6

Mauricio Pochettino addressed Manchester United fans directly on Wednesday evening after starting work officially as their new head coach

The new Red Devils head coach has promised a 'special season' in a direct message to fans

Pochettino poses at his unveiling with United director of football Jason Wilcox on Wednesday

'This is going to be a special season to support and to make our players to fight on the field and to get the results that we deserve.'

In a second message in his native Spanish, Pochettino expanded further: 'This message is about being united, like the name Manchester United. We all need to work together.

'I hope to bring the happy moments that this club deserves and create the unity that every team needs so that the players can be at their best on the pitch.'

Those messages came less than eight hours after arriving in England. He landed in Manchester at 11.32am on Wednesday and immediately headed to their Carrington training base where he took a tour and met players and staff.

Speaking to the club's media channels earlier on Wednesday, Pochettino said: 'Thank you so much, I'm very excited to be here. It's an honour, it's a privilege to be in this amazing club. I'm looking forward to starting work.'

The club then officially welcomed the new manager on their website, writing: 'Mauricio Pochettino has officially started work as Manchester United head coach, marking the start of a dream role for the Argentinian.

'Pochettino is joined at United by a team of loyal staff he has worked with at Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and USA. Join us in welcoming Jesus Perez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino.'

Pochettino had made a promise to end Man City's dominance as United manager in his last interview as United States national team coach on Tuesday evening.

He took off from northern Kentucky in a private jet chartered by the club after his final match on American soil, which saw the US beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati.

But before becoming airborne, Pochettino had time for a final statement Stateside, after being taunted that 'Manchester is blue, and will always be blue' by one of his interviewers.

Earlier on Wednesday, Pochettino made his way to Carrington straight after landing in Manchester, meeting players and staff and taking a tour

The Argentine took off from northern Kentucky in a private jet last night and landed at 11.32am

The manager shared a picture from his journey as he prepared to touch down at the airport (Source: Instagram/Mauricio Pochettino)

'No way,' he shook his head. 'You will see.'

'Give me time. Give me time and then that - that's going to change.'

Pochettino also shared a poignant farewell message to his US set-up, days after breaking down in tears in a press conference ahead of his penultimate time in charge.

Man United fans may also have been pleased to read of Pochettino's new-found love of John Denver's song Country Roads in his goodbye message, a song which is played before kick-off at Old Trafford.

'It is never easy to say goodbye, especially after everything we experienced together.' Pochettino captioned a carousel of photos of his time in the role. 'I always wanted the opportunity to coach in the USA, and I was very happy to have this chance with the national team. Two incredible years, with so many great moments and experiences that will stay with me always.

'From the challenges we faced at the Gold Cup to the excitement of the USA hosting the World Cup, and now finishing our time by reaching the semi-finals of the Nations League, I am proud of what we achieved.

'When we arrived, I wanted us to believe that we could compete with anyone. I hope today that belief is stronger, not only with the players but with everyone who supports this team. Not everything in football can be measured by results, and I believe we have helped build something important for the future of soccer in this country.

The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United

'This experience has re-energised me and given me so much, both in football and personally. I have discovered a wonderful country, made new friends and enjoyed so many of the traditions. Every time I hear Country Roads, I will forever think of all of you with a smile.

'Thank you to the players, staff, everyone at (the US national team) and all the supporters. Especially to those who believed in us and gave us this opportunity.

'Leaving is tough at this moment, but sometimes in football an opportunity comes that is impossible to say no to. I have always believed in following my heart, even when it means leaving a place where I have been very happy.

'I hope this team continues to grow and achieves all the success it deserves. Thank you USA.'

Pochettino had previously explained his emotions as stemming from how difficult the decision had been to leave the national team and re-start at Old Trafford.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said on Friday. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'

Man United first made contact with Pochettino following their breathless 4-4 draw against Aston Villa in their last match before the international break.

The Man United hierarchy had previously given former head coach Michael Carrick a stay of execution amid a worrying start to the season, but as they prepared to head into the two-week pause in the relegation zone, the board became keen to make a change.

An agonising wait for Carrick followed, with the club legend taking training for multiple sessions at the start of the week as his future was openly mulled by executives including CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

After the duo returned from Monaco, where they had flown to speak to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe about Carrick's future, the 45-year-old was finally dispatched last Thursday morning.

In their statement regarding Pochettino's arrival on Wednesday, United also confirmed the exits of Carrick and Co, writing: 'The club can confirm the departures of Travis Binnion, Jonny Evans, Steve Holland, Craig Mawson and Jonathan Woodgate alongside Michael Carrick.

'We would like to thank the group for their total commitment, dedication and professionalism, and we wish them all good luck for the future.'

Pochettino's United States farewell match went off in pitch-perfect style, which allowed thoughts to quickly move to the next task at hand after the final whistle.

Christian Pulisic helped make sure that Pochettino's reign in charge ended on a high note

The manager will now focus his attentions on getting Man United out of the relegation zone

'When you finish the game, you start in your mind to think about different things,' Pochettino said after the win. 'Of course, it's tough because it's emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything.'

Travelling with Pochettino were outgoing USMNT first-team coach Miguel D'Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott, while his assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez as well as Pochettino's son and fitness coach Sebastiano have already begun preparing for Sunday's matchup with Liverpool at Anfield.

Man United paid a staggering £10million to cleave Pochettino and his staff away from the United States, after the head coach signed a new contract with the national team in the wake of this summer's World Cup.

The quick turnaround means Pochettino will be able to work with the players as they begin reporting back from international duty. Furthermore, he is expected to speak to club media before conducting his pre-match press conference around lunchtime on Friday.

Before boarding his flight, Pochettino not only waved to his adoring fans, but took a photo with staff and players on the pitch in Cincinnati.

'It's impossible not to cry, but that is because we care about the people and the people care about us,' he told reporters. 'When that happens, it's normal to show your emotions, no? Because we are human. We are no robots.'

Wouter Vrancken remains confident Hearts can realise their “dream” of qualifying for the knockout phase of the Conference League.

The injury-hit Jambos have one point from their three matches so far as they prepare to host Monaco on Thursday before another home game against Bosnian side Borac and a trip to Cyprus to face Pafos.

In a change to the Europa League squad list, Spittal has been re-registered in place of the injured Malachi Fagan-Walcott.

“It’s very important,” Vrancken said of being able to call on Spittal, who captained the team earlier in the season. “When you looked at the injury list, they were all quality players there, and we need them all.

“And the more coming back, the better for us. Because it’s not only extra personalities, but it’s also extra quality. It gives the other players also more rest and rotation possibilities.

“So it’s all good things and we have to keep pushing. When the bodies are coming back, it’s also good for the mental side of it. For the other players who are already playing a lot of games, it’s also a good thing and it’s also good motivation.”

Vrancken hopes Landry Kabore’s double at Dundee can help the striker get back on track after what he viewed as a loss of confidence since he was substituted following a poor display in the 2-2 draw at home to Rapid Vienna in August.

“He had a difficult period,” said Vrancken. “I remember here at the home game when we brought him in and he lost every ball he had.

“But I’m just happy for him that he could cope with the situation and that he could manage to show himself in training sessions. He can be also an example for others who are in the same situation.”

#1837. Crawley Town Fan column: This was a good point, but it was touch and go at times in that second half

Player to Watch: Vito Mannone (Crawley Town)

Well, that was a tense watch. We definitely rode our luck at times, but I’ll happily take a point from a 0-0 draw with Barnet at the Broadfield Stadium. We put in an impressive defensive display, setting up with a back four with Charlie Barker sitting just in front, which allowed Josh Flint and Ben Heneghan to put in some massive clearances and blocks, which really frustrated Barnet.

Going forward, Kellan Gordon was whipping in some great crosses from the right, with  Dylan Morgan powering through midfield to cause problems, as we looked lively for most of the first half. However, it was Barnet who had the best chances, and if it wasn’t for Vito Mannone, who was great throughout the whole game, as he made some outstanding saves onto the post and crossbar to keep us in the game.

#1836. Former Geordie Guimaraes taunts Sunderland fans as Arsenal show mark of champions

Bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands. Despite the missiles, the Brazilian wore a look that made it clear he was very much enjoying his first goal in an Arsenal shirt.

Mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality. Late meals and making the dressing room hotter are among his tricks, although nothing can prepare a player having 40,000 fans calling you a “sad Geordie b------”.

So it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved. Just 121 seconds after Enzo Le Fée had his spot kick tipped on to a post by David Raya, Guimarães was rubbing salt into the wound with a stunning long-range strike that went in off the crossbar.

Enzo Le Fée is denied by David Raya from the spot 😳🧤📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/wnoMCDVh88

Bruno Guimarães silences the Stadium of Light with a BEAUTY 🥵🚀📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zQHSSLxC3o

The former Newcastle captain gave the perfect response after being taunted his old rivals. “It was a beautiful goal,” he said. “Everyone knows my past, I had an amazing history at Newcastle. But now I’m trying to create a new history here and I have started on the right foot.”

What an important week it has been for Arsenal, who have shown their squad depth by winning in Napoli then travelling to the Stadium of Light and extending their perfect start to the season to six games.

Other teams with aspirations of the title dropped points earlier in the day, while Arteta could battle to a win with key players brought back into the team and Guimarães coming off the bench at half-time. A trip in the Champions League followed by an away game the following weekend is a barometer of where teams are, and Arsenal have sounded a warning after coming through a bruising encounter.

Régis Le Bris’s team offer a challenge that is impossible to replicate, even by the standards of Arteta’s “sabotage” to make his players uncomfortable. Fans belted out Elvis Presley and 90s anthem Ready To Go just before kick-off. Then there was the aggression that Arsenal players faced. There were complaints of elbows being aimed at Gabriel Magalhães.

Bukayo Saka scored a stoppage-time penalty to seal the win but the evening belonged to Guimarães, the £75m summer signing who has been waiting for this moment to ignite his Arsenal career.

“Everyone knows I had a difficult start through injuries in my short time. But I’m glad to be back and glad to play,” Guimarães said. “I feel very good. It was unbelievable to score a beautiful goal, beautiful moment for me and my family and I am happy.”

These are ominous signs for Arsenal’s title rivals, with Guimarães’s return to fitness adding to the midfield options. Arteta’s changes to his starting line-up restored Riccardo Calafiori and Kai Havertz – two of the in-form players in the Premier League – to the team, rather than squad players being rotated.

And his players stood up to a physical challenge. Brian Brobbey used his frame to back into the Arsenal’s centre-backs, who are unlikely to given such a tough assignment this season aside from facing Erling Haaland.

Guimarães was brought on at half-time along with Jurriën Timber, which was another sign of Arsenal mounting a strong defence of their title. With Arteta’s changes altering the pace of the game, the match turned just before the hour mark. John Brooks saw nothing in the incident that floored Gabriel at a corner, but at the next set-piece penalised Ezri Konsa for wrestling with Dan Ballard, much to Arteta’s fury.

Le Fée had earned a point against Brentford a week earlier with a penalty, but this time his finish was tipped on to the post by David Raya. “We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that,” added Arteta.

“But I loved the save from David, the way the team reacted, the way we go again and we go against everything, but this should never happen, it’s not fair, and I am sad, very sad, in that sense.”

Raya also denied Nordi Mukiele from close range when Granit Xhaka’s expertly taken free-kick found his team-mate in front of goal. Sunderland have their own European campaign starting on Thursday and will start with confidence after pushing the champions all the way.

Brooks awarded a penalty in stoppage-time when Saka was brought down by Reinildo Mandava, who was dismissed. “I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place,” added Arteta.

Bukayo Saka wraps up all three points for Arsenal from the spot 🥶📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrLyrykwlh

Mikel Arteta launched a furious attack on referee John Brooks for awarding a penalty against Arsenal and fears similar decisions will cost his team the Premier League title.

Brooks gave a spot-kick for Ezri Konsa tussling with Dan Ballard, although Arteta accused the Sunderland centre-back of a “judo roll”.

Enzo Le Fée’s penalty was saved by David Raya, with Arsenal winning after goals from Bruno Guimarães and Bukayo Saka.

“In my opinion, that is not acceptable. I watched it 20 times,” said Arteta. “And I cannot find a way to understand how you think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has to intervene.

“I’m sad that we have to discuss something in such a beautiful game at this level. That has gravity because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship. And at this level, with all the work that we put in, this cannot happen.

“You see, it is a judo roll and it brings the player on the floor. So how can this happen? I cannot find an explanation. That’s why I’m trying to find that.”

The win rounded off a positive week for Arsenal despite Arteta’s fury at the officials.

“I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place. We had really good periods but didn’t score and after that they can suffocate you especially when they decided to be really physical and very direct and we had to overcome a situation that in my opinion was absolutely unacceptable at this level. I’m very worried and very sad because this can never be a penalty ever.

“Are you surprised? Are you surprised? No. OK.

“Ezri does nothing. Just watch it. We have a lot of cameras and VAR, and we have to take responsibility to protect the game. Today the game was unprotected and it could have cost us the game and the momentum which is a really, really serious thing,” he added.

“I’m making it very clear publicly because it’s for the game, it’s not only for Arsenal, this cannot happen at this level. We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that.”

Guimarães’s goal was his first for Arsenal, with Arteta adding: “Beautiful, he came on, the goal, the assist, remarkable. That why we talk about the finishers and making that impact and being able to support and help the team. He was outstanding.”

Three points or not, the Arsenal manager is furious about the penalty that was awarded to Sunderland.

I’m so upset – it’s unacceptable at this level. Unacceptable. This can change the course of a season, of the championship. I’ve seen it 10 times, to make sure, because I saw it live and said ‘It’s not possible at this level it can be a penalty’. Because it’s a judo roll, that’s what it is. It cannot happen.

I’ve been in football for 27 or 28 years - it’s not a penalty in any game, in any league, in any context.

Sunderland are a really, really good team and I don’t want to take any credit away from them. It’s been extremely tough and I’m really happy that we’ve done it.

"It's not a penalty in any case, in any game, in any context, in any league" 😳Mikel Arteta reflects on Arsenal's 2-0 win over Sunderland 👀@jules_breach | 📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/2BUZILexk3

I feel very good. It was a beautiful goal and a beautiful moment for me and my family.

It’s a very good place to score! Everyone knows my history at Newcastle; now I’m trying to create more history with Arsenal.

[Is David Raya the best goalkeeper in the world?] Definitely. This guy’s an unbelievable player.

What a goal! And especially the time he scored. Coming to this place is so difficult but we dealt with it very well.

It’s a big moment, especially at 0-0 away from home, and they were on top of us at the time.

"What a goal, and especially the time that he scored" 🙌David Raya and Bruno Guimarães reflect on their win over Sunderland this evening 🤝@jules_breach | 📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mozUB0mFd8

Arsenal have won nine Premier League games in a row for the first since the Invincible season of 2003-04.

Three away games for Arsenal this season, three wins and three clean sheets. Nobody does it better. The Arsenal players will sleep well tonight because Sunderland made them work extremely hard for the three points.

The match was decided by a dramatic three-minute period early in the second half. Enzo Le Fee’s penalty was superbly saved by David Raya; then the Arsenal substitute – and former Newcastle captain – Bruno Guimares slammed a spectacular goal.

Bukayo Saka confirmed victory with an injury-time penalty. Arsenal are top of the table with 12 points out of 12; good luck trying to catch them.

90+7 min: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 2 (Saka pen) Bukayo Saka’s penalty goes through the hands of the diving Roefs and into the net. That should be the last kick of the game.

Bukayo Saka wraps up all three points for Arsenal from the spot 🥶📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrLyrykwlh

90+6 min: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 1 Saka is fouled by Reinildo, whose misery is compounded by a second yellow card.

Gabriel and Mukiele are booked for their part in that shoving match.

There’s a bit of pushing and shoving from players on both sides after a foul by Isidor on Guimaraes. Nothing much in it.

Sunderland have six minutes of added time in which to find an equaliser.

Arsenal substitution Mikel Merino for Martin Odegaard, presumably for his height at defensive set-pieces.

Big save from Raya! Xhaka takes a corner on the right, gets it back and curls another wicked ball into the six-yard box. Mukiele stretches to poke it towards goal and Raya paws the ball away. It loops up invitingly in front of goal - but then Raya is fouled by one of the Sunderland players charging desperately towards the ball.

A Sunderland corner loops up in the air and is volleyed acrobatically over the bar by Mukiele. That was a pretty good effort, and it only just cleared the bar.

Double change for Arsenal Eberechi Eze and Martin Zubimendi replace Christos Tzolis and... Declan Rice. He doesn’t look injured so it might just be workload management.

Brobbey pushes Gabriel over off the ball and is booked.

Disallowed goal Odegaard’s beautiful free-kick is headed in emphatically by Timber - but then the flag goes up for offside. Not much in it but the decision has been confirmed.

Sunderland substitution Malick Fofana replaces Thomas Meunier and creates a chance immediately with a thrilling run down the left. There’s an appeal for a penalty and then a close-range backheel from Mukiele that is blocked by Konsa.

Ballard clears off the line! Saka swings the resulting corner to the far post, where Havertz rises imperiously to head past Roefs. Ballard stoops towards his own goal and heads clear superbly. I’m not entirely sure Havertz’s header was on target but Ballard didn’t know that.

Moments later, Guimaraes curls just wide of the far post.

Fine save by Roefs! Arsenal cut Sunderland open on the break. Tzolis flicks a neat pass to Odegaard, who runs at a backpedalling defence and tees up Saka. His right-foot shot is beaten round the post by Roefs.

Eyebrows were raised at the £75m fee for Bruno Guimaraes, especially as he turns 29 in November, but Arsenal were willing to pay so much money because they knew the Brazilian was a sure thing. Only a player with serious experience of the Premier League could come into central midfield, off the bench, in a game like this and completely understand the tempo and flow of the game.

Sunderland substitution Wilson Isidor replaces Nilson Angulo.

Xhaka is booked for a sliding tackle on Guimaraes, though he got the ball and felt it was a clean challenge.

Chance for Arsenal Saka puts Havertz through on goal on the left side of the area. He eschews the shot and instead tries to find Tzolis with a square pass that is cut out by a Sunderland defender. Havertz may have been too selfless there.

Dan Ballard is booked - not sure whether it was a foul or for dissent.

The home fans have been stunned into relative silence by that double whammy. It was a mighty finish from Bruno Guimaraes.

58 min: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 1 (Guimaraes) A hammer blow from the former Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes! Sunderland looked set to go 1-0 up a moment ago; now they’re 1-0 down. Rice played a square pass to Guimaraes, lurking with intent just outside the D; he got the ball out of his feet and whipped an unstoppable curler into the top corner. What a way - and time, and place - to score your first Arsenal goal.

Bruno Guimarães silences the Stadium of Light with a BEAUTY 🥵🚀📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zQHSSLxC3o

55 min: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 0 A fantastic save from David Raya, who springs to his left and touches Enzo Le Fee’s penalty onto the post! Sensational goalkeeping!

Enzo Le Fée is denied by David Raya from the spot 😳🧤📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/wnoMCDVh88

54 min: Sunderland 0 Arsenal 0 A long throw from the left is claimed by David Raya - but the referee points to the spot after a wrestling manoeuvre by Konsa on Ballard!

Arsenal are furious, and that probably wouldn’t have been given last season, but clubs were told at the start of the season that wrestling would be penalised.

Gabriel goes down holding his jaw and claims he was elbowed by Ballard. VAR aren’t interested and the referee tells an irritated Gabriel to leave the field for one minute.

Konsa makes an important challenge on the relentless Brobbey, as does Gabriel on Le Fee a few seconds later. Sunderland keep pushing and Sadiki rakes a shot over the bar from the edge of the area.

Chance for Sunderland A long throw from the right isn’t cleared by Arsenal, and eventually Meunier hits a snapshot that is kicked away instinctively by David Raya. That’s a pretty good save.

Jurrien Timber and Bruno Guimaraes, who is popular in these parts, replace Ben White and Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Tzolis’s deep cross is headed back into the six-yard box by Saka. Havertz stoops towards the ball but is beaten to it by Xhaka, a crucial bit of defending and the last action of a hard-fought, goalless first half.

Ben White has a groin problem and is going to be replaced by Jurrien Timber, either now or at half-time.

Xhaka’s dangerous corner is punched back to him by Raya. He picks out Le Fee, who drags a shot wide of the near post from 20 yards. Sunderland’s belief is growing.

Angulo goes down in the Arsenal area after a challenge from the side by White. Play continues and Meunier’s speuclative shot deflects behind for a corner.

Sunderland have been terrific in this first half.

Mikel Arteta is booked for encroaching outside his technical area. He responds by sticking his thumb up at the fourth official.

Mikel Arteta receives a yellow card for stepping out of the technical area 😅📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/xDlnL1B9MY

Arsenal are yet to score from a set piece this season. Their supporters have used that fact as evidence they are not as reliant on corners as their critics say, but the truth is that it will bother Arteta and set-piece coach Nicolas Jover. This is the sort of cagey game in which Arsenal so often made the breakthrough from a set piece last season.

Sunderland break through Mukiele, who charges into space and rifles a low drive that is blocked by Gabriel on the edge of the area.

The resulting corner leads to a brief VAR check for an Arsenal penalty after a bit of a wrestling match between Calafiori and Brobbey. Nothing given.

Good save by Roefs Saka curls a cross towards Havertz, who does well to control it on the chest while facing away from goal. He waits for the ball to bounce and hooks an imaginative shot that is fingertipped over by Roefs. Good save.

Chance for Arsenal Tzolis plays a nice pass down the side of the area for Odegaard. He cuts the ball back to Havertz, who screws a first-time shot over the bar. It was a slightly awkward chance because of the angle of Odegaard’s pass.

Reinildo is booked for a foul on Saka. The home fans are getting annoyed with what they perceive as diving from some of the Arsenal attackers: “Same old Arsenal, always cheating” is the chant of choice just now. Odegaard also went down a moment ago after a foul from Angulo.

Gabriel strides forward from defence and sweeps a left-foot shot from 25 yards. It’s a good effort that fades just wide of the far post with Roefs scrambling across his line.

Sunderland will be really pleased with the first quarter. They’re defending solidly and look a threat on the break, thanks in part to some outstanding hold-up play from Brian Brobbey. Saka’s volley is the only shot on target at either end.

Chance for Sunderland Brobbey does brilliantly to hold the ball and find Le Fee, who is fouled on the left wing by Gabriel. That allows Sunderland to send the centre-backs forward - and one of them, Dan Ballard, almost opens the scoring!

Xhaka curled a sensational ball around the Arsenal defence towards the far post, where the ball bounced up awkwardly and was knocked wide by either Ballard or Mukiele, who flew in at the far post. Ballard would have had an easier chance had Mukiele not got in the way.

Chance for Arsenal Saka mishits a volley straight at Roefs from close range after running onto a penetrative pass from Rice. It wasn’t an easy ball to take on the volley - Rice hit it very firmly - but Saka would usually do better.

The pattern of the game has been established, with Arsenal dominating the ball and Sunderland picking their moments to press and then counter-attack.

Looks like it will be a good battle between Brian Brobbey and Ezri Konsa. Brobbey seems to be attaching himself to Konsa, rather than getting into a scrap with Gabriel.

Sunderland break promisingly down the right. Mukiele drives an angled low cross that only just evades Angulo at the far post.

Calafiori has a shot from 18 yards blocked after a typical run infield from left-back.

Enzo Le Fee tries to score from inside his own half. David Raya was outside the penalty area but Le Fee completely mishit the shot.

Arsenal have started well and are dominating possession. So far it’s all been in front of the Sunderland defence, but you’d expect that to change if they continue to have this much of the ball.

The champions kick off from left to right as we watch.

There’s a pulsating atmosphere at the Stadium of Light - you’d expect nothing less - and the action is about to begin.

Myles Lewis Skelly is the first England teenager to start the first four league games of a season for Arsenal since Tony Adams and David Rocastle in the 1986/87 campaign.

We’re in a congested period right now. We’re playing midweek games as well. We made four changes against Napoli, we make another four for today and we try to keep all the players connected with a high level of confidence, and with the right chemistry in and around the team.

We know how tough Sunderland made it for every opponent here [last season] and we know the beautiful atmosphere that they create, the organisation that they have and the individuals that they have. We’ll try to impose ourselves like we always do and come here and be as dominant as we’ve been and then be ready to win the game.

Arsenal’s biggest rivals are still waiting for their first win - and their first goal - of the Premier League season. Alex Connor has reaction to their 0-0 draw at home to Everton.

"For sure we can improve, and we will" 😅Mikel Arteta on Arsenal's strong start to the season 🗣️📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nDpwooZq4Y

Arsenal keeper David Raya has conceded only one goal in five matches this season, but he was beaten twice on this ground last season during a thrilling 2-2 draw.

When will Martin Zubimendi start again for Arsenal? Mikel Arteta wants to avoid a repeat of last season, when Zubimendi played more games than anyone in Europe, but it is curious that the Spaniard has not yet started a single match of this campaign. It is one thing to reduce his minutes, and another to turn him into a permanent substitute.

Zubimendi has looked quite good off the bench in recent games but has been behind Myles Lewis-Skelly and Mikel Merino in the battle to partner Declan Rice from the start. And that’s before Bruno Guimaraes, the new £75m signing, reaches full fitness.

In the thick Naples air in midweek, Declan Rice did what he always does: he kept running. Another start for the Arsenal midfielder, another 90 minutes completed and another performance of constructive passing and destructive defending. For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

After that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he said.

The key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. This, after all, is a footballer who managed nerve pain in his hamstring throughout the second half of last season.

Regis Le Bris, who made 11 changes for the League Cup win over Hull in midweek, reverts to the starting XI that drew at Brentford seven days ago.

RLB's XI to take on Arsenal! ❤️👊#SUNARS pic.twitter.com/F1nXWky4Fp

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the Arsenal team that won in Napoli during the week. Kai Havertz’s return is the headline news in Arteta’s selection, with in-form left-back Riccardo Calafiori also returning. Myles Lewis-Skelly returns to the midfield and Christos Tzolis starts.

🟡 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🔵 Your Saturday night Gunners ❤️‍🔥🤝 Presented by @deel

Hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

There’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” said Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

#1835. Opposition insight for Milan-Frosinone: Form, injuries, predicted XI and more

AC Milan are looking to make it three consecutive wins tomorrow, but a high-flying newcomer in Frosinone could make that difficult.

Ruben Amorim and his men have an opportunity to really establish some momentum tomorrow evening, picking up where they left off before the break. However, it won’t be an easy game against Massimiliano Alvani’s Frosinone, who have impressed everyone so far.

Amorim even warned in his press conference that it will be a difficult one, especially since the Canarini have such a direct style.

➤ Manager: Massimiliano Alvini ➤ Form (all comps): W-D-W-W-L (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Serie A): Raimondo – 8 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Kvernadze, Schmid and Ghedjemis – 4 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: Bracaglia, Grillitsch and Raimondo.

Frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

They are currently on 20 points after eleven games, winning six, drawing two and losing three, which has put them in sixth place. That’s very strong for a newcomer and for a coach who is only in his second season with the club, especially considering the upset against Como.

It’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

So, what is behind this rise? As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, the direct style of play has been key for Frosinone. As opposed to Milan, who want to see a lot of the ball, they are willing to have less possession and break on the counter.

It doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

While collective effort deserves most of the praise, it has definitely helped that the likes of Giacomo Calo, Giorgi Kvernadze and Antonio Raimondo – among others – have performed at a very high level. They aren’t exactly big-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

Moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

The Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.

Predicted bench: Desplanches, Pisseri, Cittadini, Tchato, Amey, Akpoguma, Fayed, El Azzouzi, Cichella, Hasa, Fini, Zerbin, Bobcek.

#1834. Charalampos Kostoulas identifies Brighton turning point under Fabian Hurzeler after James Milner trust

Brighton striker Charalampos Kostoulas believes earning the trust of his teammates has been just as important as his goals this season.

The 19-year-old has made an encouraging start to the 2026-27 campaign, with five goals and three assists in 14 appearances across all competitions as he establishes himself as an increasingly important figure in Fabian Hurzeler's side.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

It marks a significant step forward from his first season at the Amex Stadium, when he scored twice in 21 Premier League appearances, making just two starts.

Brighton head coach Hurzeler - who last season questioned Kostoulas’ commitment to training - is now impressed by the progress, particularly the forward's growing physical strength, work rate and understanding of the demands of English football.

But Kostoulas says there has been no dramatic change to his game. Instead, he has gradually learned what the team requires from him and become more comfortable in his role.

"Mainly, it's about understanding what the team wants," he said to Sussex World.

"For me, as a striker, with time and after some months, I started to understand that. With the minutes I've got and things like that, I gained the trust of my teammates and I want to keep going like that."

Hurzeler has previously highlighted the difference in the youngster's ability to compete physically, saying: "When you see him now and how resilient he is in personal duels, it's something completely different."

The Brighton boss has also praised his pressing and attitude towards improvement, describing a player who is becoming increasingly professional.

Kostoulas credits the manager's clarity and attention to detail, while revealing he has enjoyed the greater freedom given to him in the attacking role.

"He's clear with the instructions he gives on the pitch. He's always clear," he said.

"But I think I didn't change the way I was playing. Last season I could also do these types of things on the pitch, but I have more of a free role, especially in my position. I like it."

The transition from Olympiacos to Brighton was not without its challenges, however.

Kostoulas admits the biggest adjustment was the daily routine, with longer hours at the training ground, different training methods and a greater emphasis on meetings and preparation.

"The daily routine, I think, was the hardest," he told Sussex World. "We spend many hours at the training ground, more than I was used to in Greece.

"There are different types of training, a different approach to the game, more meetings and things like that."

He was helped by some of Brighton's more experienced players, with former midfielder James Milner playing a particularly important role during his first season.

"Most of the older players would come and say something to me as advice," Kostoulas explained. "Last season, James Milner was speaking a lot to me and trying to help me."

He still occasionally speaks to Milner, while Pascal Gross has also become an important figure in his development.

For Kostoulas, having someone to turn to is vital when moving to a different country and footballing culture.

"It's important to have someone to help you understand the way the team works here," he explained to Sussex World.

"It's totally different. If someone from here moves to Greece, they will also need time. It will be hard for them.

"You have to find someone you can trust, have a good relationship with, speak to and who can give you an understanding of most of the things here and what's expected."

There is also the prospect of sharing the pitch with fellow Greek forward Stefanos Tsitsimas, whose return from a lengthy spell out has delighted Kostoulas.

"I'm really happy for him," he said. "He has a really good mindset and I have big trust in him. I think he will do great."

Kostoulas was keen to avoid looking too far ahead when asked about Brighton's ambitions after their impressive start to the season.

Rather than focus on the possibility of challenging at the top of the table or making a deep run in Europe, he insists the squad are concentrating on the next match.

"We don't think about what will happen after six months when the season will be finished," he said to Sussex World.

"We're just enjoying every day, trying to be happy and win as many games as we can."

#1833. Who are Pluto Data Analytics? Celtic take leaf from Hearts in bid to enhance player recruitment

Celtic have taken a leaf from the Hearts model by taking the plunge into the world of data analytics.

The Scottish champions have announced a strategic partnership with Pluto Data Analytics in a bid to enhance their player recruitment.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The link-up with the London-based football analytics and predictive modelling company will initially run for three years, with scope for it to be extended.

Celtic’s recruitment strategy has been heavily criticised among supporters in recent seasons amid their struggles in Europe and increased domestic competition from Rangers and Hearts.

The club said that working with Pluto would allow them to “gain access to enhanced analytical tools and insights to support existing recruitment and football operations functions”.

The move comes two years after Premiership rivals Hearts partnered with Tony Bloom-linked Jamestown Analytics in a deal which helped elevate the Edinburgh club to a level where they were within minutes of winning the title last term.

Announcing their new partnership on Wednesday, Celtic said: “The objective is clear: to improve decision-making, identify emerging opportunities and support the club’s long-term football strategy.”

Hoops chief executive Michael Nicholson stated: “We are always looking for ways to strengthen our football operation and ensure that we continue to evolve in an increasingly competitive environment. We have been reviewing the options in this area in order to select the optimum model for our club.

“Our partnership with Pluto Data Analytics, an organisation with real quality and pedigree within this field, reflects our commitment to innovation and continuous improvement.

“Recruitment remains one of the most important areas of any football club. Our aim is to identify talent as effectively as possible, reduce uncertainty where we can and support our football staff with the best available information.

“We believe this partnership will strengthen our ability to support the Club’s ambitions both domestically and in European competition.”

Manager Martin O’Neill said: “While football is not an exact science, if the club can access and utilise new tools and new details, ultimately, we hope that such data will help us deliver the success we are all striving for.

“Our recruitment and wider football operations teams have already engaged with Pluto. Our plans in the short, medium and longer term are being developed and we are confident that our relationship will deliver real tangible benefit to the club over the next few years.”

Jon Godfrey, CEO of Pluto Data Analytics, said: “We believe that predictive data modelling combined with the allure and resources of such a famous institution will allow us to achieve great things in this partnership.

“Celtic has the capacity to compete at the highest levels of European football and it is an honour and a fantastic challenge to work relentlessly with the club on achieving the exciting goals we have put in place.”

Formed in 2020, the company has between 51 and 200 employees, according to its LinkedIn profile, with its office based at Tintagel House, Albert Embankment, London.

While Jamestown Analytics were well known in football circles when they arrived on the scene at Hearts due to their previous work with Brighton and Union Saint-Gilloise, much less is known about Pluto Data Analytics.

Under the 'What We Do' section on their company website, it states: "At Pluto, we combine sports intuition with the latest technology and big data sets to answer difficult questions across multiple sports. Our work goes beyond validating player performance: we help clubs find overlooked talent, assess tactical impact and make smarter decisions at every level of the game. From top-tier recruitment to identifying emerging stars in under-scouted leagues, we turn complexity into clarity through intelligent, fast and adaptable data tools."

Another section of their website, under Bespoke Recruitment, adds: "At Pluto, we use advanced machine learning to validate how a player might adapt in a new league. For example, how would a defender in Japan’s J1 League perform in the MLS in America? This kind of insight supports clubs to make smarter, more confident recruitment decisions across borders."

Celtic are currently the only football club publicly identified as a client of Pluto Data Analytics, although the company states on its website that its predictive models are used by "clubs around the globe".

Like Jamestown, Pluto also has a background in the betting market, with their website stating: "Our models have been battle-tested by clients in betting markets, validating our edge across multiple sports."

In another similarity, Pluto’s CEO, Jon Godfrey, is a former professional poker. Tony Bloom, who founded Jamestown Analytics, also played poker professionally although there is no record of the pair having crossed paths.
