#1776. Arsenal's complacency and a lack of ambition allowed Newcastle a way back and the Gunners were fortunate to escape with a point after paying the price for not killing the game, writes CRAIG HOPE

Published: 15:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026

Do not invite the hostility, Arsenal were warned. Do not prod the bear. Do not start Bruno Guimaraes. The champions, with a belligerence of their own, ignored all of that and put the grizzly to sleep in a typically smothering first half. Their mistake was in thinking it was dead.

And so, awakened by a half-time rocket from head coach Matthias Jaissle - including three, inspirational changes - Newcastle somehow led by the 62nd minute.

By this point, the two teams were unrecognisable from those who had played out a one-sided opening period, after which Arsenal were 1-0 in front. Mikel Arteta would not have settled for a draw then.

‘We were exceptional in the first half,’ he later said. ‘We have won matches playing much worse than we did here. The intensity, the aggression – we should have been 3-0 or 4-0 up. But right from the start of the second half, we weren’t at the races. We lost duels, gave the ball away and gave them belief.’

Arteta had Noni Madueke to thank for rescuing the point. The winger was his best player throughout and, had he earlier shown the same incision that produced his 78th-minute equaliser, Arsenal would have won. They would have won by half-time, in fact.

So dominant were they, maybe it was complacency. Or maybe there is a lesson here in showing more bloodthirst when on top.

Arteta, you feel, gets more of a kick from suffocating opponents. But during a pulsating second half in which St James’ Park throbbed to the beat of their brilliant team, the hosts grabbed the pillowcase.

Noni Madueke saved Arsenal's blushes with an equaliser against Newcastle in a tough second half on Saturday

‘The second half was pure belief, pure conviction, pure trust in the team-mate,’ said Jaissle, under increased scrutiny amid the presence of chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan.

‘There were so many ball-wins with a vertical approach and causing them problems. This is the Newcastle DNA.’

Former Newcastle captain Guimaraes - booed after each of his 36, ineffectual touches - was hooked in the 70th minute, and Arsenal were better for their own changes.

The league leaders can absorb this result, of course. Of greater concern for Arteta is an injury to David Raya that requires an MRI scan.

The goalkeeper left the pitch at the same time as Guimaraes, not because of performance, but clutching his shoulder, the upshot of a robust challenge from William Osula. That home forcefulness typified their second half, if not their first.

The Magpies were poor in the first period but a half-time team talk and changes from Matthias Jaissle worked wonders

Bruno Guimaraes earned a hostile reception as he returned to face the side he once captained

There is now concern for the Gunners, with goalkeeper David Raya going off injured

If Newcastle were to beat Arsenal, so suggested the crumbs of pre-match optimism, they would have to start fast.

At least, that was the blueprint of old on red-hot nights such as this. Newcastle started slow. Arsenal weren’t much quicker, but they didn’t have to be. They moved through the gears as the half unfolded and, with it, they began to move through Newcastle.

Arteta likes this sort of game, when it feels like minimum expenditure for maximum return. In short, it was easy. A training-ground drill. Attack versus defence.

Come half-time, Newcastle had not touched the ball in Arsenal’s penalty area. They simply weren’t allowed to.

Saying that, even with permission they would have found a way to pass it straight out of play or shank a cross into the Leazes End.

Newcastle’s first half really was that short on inspiration. There wasn’t too much perspiration, either. And so the home fans booed on the whistle, for a fifth half on the spin at St James’.

NEWCASTLE (4-3-3): Hornicek 5; Dedic 5 (Livramento 46, 7), Thiaw 7, Burn 7, Hall 6 (Botman 90); Miley 7, Steur 6 (Ramsey 46, 7); Murphy 5 (Elanga 46, 6), Willock 7 (Wissa 83), Barnes 7; Osula 6

ARSENAL (4-2-3-1): Raya 5 (Arrizabalaga 70, 5); Timber 6, Konsa 6, Gabriel 6, Calafiori 6; Guimaraes 5 (Lewis-Skelly 70, 7), Rice 6; Madueke 8, Odegaard 7 (Merino 90), Eze 6 (Tzolis 70, 6); Havertz 7 (Gyokeres 90)

Arsenal led by one, and for them that should have been a source of regret.

The goal came when Lewis Hall, despite screams from team-mate Dan Burn to ‘head it, head it’, decided to control, clumsily, on his chest, allowing Kai Havertz to steal. He freed Eberechi Eze and the first-time finish was routine.

The punishment of Hall’s error, however, was ruthless. Six days after bettering Lamine Yamal, England left back Hall was struggling to contain Madueke. In fact, he and each of his comrades could not get close to any of those in red.

So, it was as if two sides had swapped shirts after the break. From nowhere, Newcastle attacked. That may sound basic, but this was seismic. The exclusion zone that had been Arsenal’s penalty box was no longer off limits.

Suddenly, they were able to run, tackle and, yes, shoot. From passive to aggressive, they drew level just four minutes after the restart.

Joe Willock hurried Odegaard into a mistake, William Osula pounced on the loose ball and, when Harvey Barnes was set free, he was not going to miss.

The turnaround was complete when defender Malick Thiaw forced over the goal-line from a corner which Arsenal had failed to defend - Dan Burn’s free header told you that someone, somewhere was not doing their job.

'We needed players with more energy and physicality,’ said Jaissle, explaining his half-time changes.

‘The tactics did not change, it was purely the front footed behaviour. Throw away the doubts, then you saw what is possible. We had Arsenal shaking. I hope we can carry on this feeling.’

Newcastle looked the most likely winners until Madueke burst inside two home jerseys and fired through Lukas Hornicek from 18 yards. Still, the hosts came back for more.

Arsenal had arrived intent on silencing St James’. In the end, they were grateful for the sound of the full-time whistle.

#1774. Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town

There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn

At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x

As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a new contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

“A joy to have him,” said Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

“Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta says Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z

Dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” said Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”

Dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

It was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” said Arteta.

Arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

Given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

The only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

Akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub

On managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta said: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady says Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf

Asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta said: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”

He added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta said: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

“Individually some big performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”

Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).

Their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).

No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.

It has meant that Gary O’Neil has had to leave established players out of match-day squads. “It was really tough leaving out Darnell [Furlong] and Anis [Mehmeti] from the squad [against Crystal Palace],” he said. “Doing that to good people is one of the toughest parts of the job. But I have faith in them, it’s just that everyone’s fit at the moment and we’ve had to recruit a strong squad to get us through an unbelievably challenging season.

“On Tuesday, whoever I pick, I have 100 per cent faith that they’re ready and that they’re going to represent what we do and how we go about it.”

On Hincapie’s omission from the match-day squad:

“Some players were carrying some fatigue, some little issues that we have to look after and some other players are available, fresh and in better conditions to play.

On Timber being left out of tonight’s squad:

“Everything is fine, but obviously he has played much more than we would have wanted. He played 53 minutes [against Sunderland] after five months. I will need to look after him.”

When asked if Arsenal will set up with a back three tonight:

Alan Davies, the actor and comedian who is a famously passionate supporter of Arsenal, recently told a story about a charity event he once attended with former captain Tony Adams. Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies said Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”

The “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams said, everything else flows from there.

For much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.

Tonight will be a good test for young Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who is the latest high-class graduate of the Arsenal academy. Arsenal have extremely high hopes for Salmon, who made four senior appearances last season. He could be in the centre of defence or at right-back tonight. I suspect Ipswich striker Zian Flemming might try to target Salmon with some physical challenges, especially in the air. Let’s see how he handles it.

Substitutes Meslier, Calafiori, Konsa, Tzolis, Odegaard, Ibrahim, Julienne, Saka, Havertz

Max Dowman announced himself last season, showing off his gilded footwork in impressive cameos off the bench. Who could forget that lung-busting run and goal against Everton?

And while the 16-year-old winger featured in Arsenal’s pre-season, these will be his first minutes of senior football in the season proper. His only game time thus far has come in the Premier League 2 under-21s competition and he was not included in the match-day squad at the Stadium of Light on Saturday.

When asked about Dowman after the victory at Sunderland, Arteta said: “I wish we could have him here, but we have the limitation with the numbers that we can have. He will have his chance, he will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else. We know the talent that we have, we know the players that we have there and we need to help him and find a way to make sure he continues to develop and help the team.”

Although keeping Ipswich in the Premier League must be Gary O’Neil’s primary goal, he has insisted that the club will embrace opportunities in the cups.

When asked how he would approach tonight’s tie, O’Neil said: “We’ll have a strong side, we’ve worked our socks off in the transfer window to give ourselves a strong squad. Of course, a different level to Arsenal, but we’ll be strong on Tuesday and we’ll do our best to win the game.

“The club has worked so hard to have these moments and of course it’s a cup game, but to have Arsenal and Liverpool come to Portman Road a week or so apart is what everyone has worked so hard for in recent years, so we’re going to enjoy it, we’re going to have a right go and worst thing that can happen is we lose to Arsenal.”

Good evening from Portman Road, where it’s a gorgeous night for football. Ipswich have made 10 changes, which is an indication of where this competition sits in their list of priorities. Arsenal have made nine.

The Arsenal line-up is quite hard to decipher. It looks like it might be Martin Zubimendi at right-back or centre-back. I’ll keep an eye on the warm-ups and report back shortly.

Gary O’Neil wins the rotation battle, raising Arteta’s nine changes with 10 of his own. Greaves the only survivor from last weekend’s win at Selhurst Park.

Your Town tonight! ✊ pic.twitter.com/EEYjPFww4Y

Young defender Marli Salmon comes into the starting XI as Mikel Arteta makes nine changes to the team that started against Sunderland on Saturday.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Introducing your Carabao Cup Gunners starting XI ✨🤝 @deel

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Ipswich Town and Arsenal. Mikel Arteta’s side have won all six of their matches so far this season, but travel to Portman Road fresh off an incident-filled win over Sunderland which thrust officiating back into the spotlight after Ezri Konsa conceded a penalty having been – in Arteta’s words – “judo-rolled” by Dan Ballard.

After the match, the Arsenal manager said: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”

Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.

This season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. This would likely mean starting Jurriën Timber, who is only just returning from a long-term groin issue. There is more scope for rotation in advanced positions, with Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino contenders to start.

A 90th-minute Zian Flemming winner against Crystal Palace on Saturday helped Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich to their second win in four Premier League games, a feat they required 16 matches to achieve the last time they were in the top flight. Heavy investment into Ipswich’s squad has proved fruitful thus far, though in-form striker Emersonn is expected to sit out tonight having taken a knock at Selhurst Park.

#1773. A potential audition and the scorers from midfield: The five key battles in Milan vs. Frosinone

AC Milan resume their Serie A campaign after the final international break on 2026 by welcoming Frosinone to San Siro.

Ruben Amorim’s side are in need of a win to climb back into the top four after Como’s result on Saturday, while Roma and Lazio also picked up victories. They face a Frosinone team who will be full of confidence after an excellent start to their campaign, following promotion in 2025-26.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The latest team news suggests that Amorim will go with a 4-4-1-1 formation, though in his pre-match press conference he did not give too much away about his selection choices, especially in view of Thursday’s trip to Greece.

At the risk of sounding like a broken record, something simply has to click for Goncalo Ramos, and preferably soon. He has gone one month without a goal and his struggles to even generate shots followed him to Portugal on international duty. However, Frosinone are a side that score goals but also let them in too, so there should be spaces to exploit.

It will be an intriguing battle between the No.9 and Gabriele Calvani, while it could even be an audition of sorts for the centre-back. Milan have been linked with the Genoa loanee, who has made an impressive start to the campaign, so it will be an up-close look as he tries to pile the misery on Ramos.

With top scorer Antonio Raimondo out injured, Giorgi Kvernadze will be the main goal threat for the away side. The Georgian’s seven goal contributions are only bettered by the Italian striker, and he has started all 11 games under Alvini so far in Serie A.

It seems that Mario Gila will be tasked with stopping Kvernadze. The Spaniard spent the break at Milanello after not being called up by Spain again, and he should slot in as the right-sided defender again next to Koni De Winter.

Moving into midfield, there will be a fascinating contest between Adrien Rabiot and Giacomo Calo. It starts with a very obvious point of comparison: both are known for their goal scoring prowess, with the Frenchman already on five for the season and the Italian having racked up the same number.

The pair are likely to face each other head-to-head too. Whereas Rabiot has usually played deeper like Calo, it seems that the head coach is thinking of moving him further forward to play behind Ramos, so he will see a lot of Calo and also Patrizio Masini.

Alvini is expected to give the nod to Aleksa Terzic at left-back, which is notable because the Serbian has only started one game so far in 2026-27, with his other four appearances all coming off the bench. He does like to get forward in transition though, and has a goal to his name.

Primarily, Terzic will be tasked with trying to limit Diego Moreira’s impact on the game. The Belgian – who scored for his national team for the first time in their rout of Italy – is expected to start on the right for the Rossoneri, and his seven goal contributions in seven games tell their own story.

Finally, we return to the middle of the park where Luka Modric and Romano Schmid will headline as series of interesting duels. Modric’s importance to Milan in all phases of the game have been written about at length, but particularly the build-up phase in games where his team are expected to dominate the ball.

The Croatian is the metronome for the Rossoneri just as the summer signing Schmid is for the Canarini. The Austrian has been playing mostly as an attacking midfielder, with two goals and four assists to his name, and starts in all 11 rounds thus far.

#1772. Raheem Sterling dodges prison for dangerously driving Lamborghini

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Former England footballer Raheem Sterling, 31, has been handed a suspended prison sentence today.

He was sentenced to 12 months in prison, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court after dangerously driving his Lamborghini and possessing nitrous oxide canisters.

Sterling was also ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid work and was banned from driving for 24 months.

He had been seen by other motorists inhaling from a balloon while driving his black sports car, swerving in and out of lanes – with one driver ‘shocked’ by what he saw, a court previously heard.

Sterling arrived at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court this morning, wearing a black top and dark trousers.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

He has been on unconditional bail and subject to an interim driving ban since he admitted offences in September.

The former Manchester City player had pleaded guilty at the Hampshire court to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before he crashed on the morning of May 28.

Sterling also admitted possession of six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.

Police body-worn footage of the footballer’s arrest at 9.15am shows him in the crashed car with two canisters on his lap as the officer tells him: ‘You can put that down mate.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The court previously heard witness Christopher Jennings on the M25 called 999 at 7.49am after he was driving in parallel to Sterling’s car and ‘he was shocked by what he saw’.

Sterling scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate’s side reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the final of Euro 2020.

He came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut.

Sterling, who was born in Kingston, Jamaica, moved to Manchester City in 2015 and won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup in 2019.

He left for Chelsea in 2022 but, after falling out of favour, spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal.

After leaving Stamford Bridge, Sterling joined Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of the season.

Sterling was made an MBE in the 2021 Queen’s Birthday Honours for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out against racism on and off the pitch for several years.

It came amid controversy over England fans booing players taking the knee at matches as a gesture against intolerance.

#1770. Mikel Arteta issues new David Raya injury update ahead of Arsenal vs Man City

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta provided a coy update on David Raya’s availability for Arsenal’s showdown with Manchester City this weekend.

The goalkeeper missed the Gunners’ draw with Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night with a shoulder injury that he picked up against Newcastle.

The Spaniard left the pitch at St James’ Park in significant pain and Arsenal feared a lengthy absence, but scans proved to be positive.

The No1 has avoided a serious injury and he will not require surgery, though there is uncertainty over exactly when he will return.

There are suggestions that the goalkeeper will only be out for a matter of days and could be in contention to face City on Sunday.

“No, we have nothing to add today unfortunately,” Arteta said after his side’s 1-1 draw with Dortmund.

“We need to know first how bad it is and whether he has a chance or not [to face Man City].”

In Raya’s absence, Kepa Arrizabalaga started against Dortmund, as Arsenal had to settle for just a point despite a dominant performance.

The Spaniard was fairly comfortable throughout, though he did have some shaky moments from corners and when rolling the ball out to Myles Lewis-Skelly to play him into trouble.

However, it was an improvement on Kepa’s display in the Carabao Cup final last season and solid enough to be confident he will keep his place over Illan Meslier while Raya remains out.

Kepa has had limited football since joining the club, so trusted has Raya become for Arsenal, but Arteta insisted he will have full faith in the goalkeeper if he is required to start in goal against City.

“Him and Illan, they’re both in the same situation,” Arteta said.

“I think Kepa had a really good performance today. We fully trust our keepers and if he needs to play against City, he will play.”

United made a disappointing start to life under their new head coach Mauricio Pochettino, shipping four goals as they fell to a dispiriting defeat against Liverpool.

The scale of the task at hand will now be all the more apparent to Pochettino, with his side now winless in nine Premier League matches and just one point off bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace.

The upcoming January transfer window may provide a precious opportunity for United to add some much-needed defensive depth to their squad.

#1768. GdS: ‘If not the best’ – Cardinale accelerates by publicly declaring Milan’s Endrick admiration

A rather significant step was taken on Saturday, as Gerry Cardinale publicly declared AC Milan’s interest in signing Endrick.

La Gazzetta dello Sport have revealed that Cardinale spent six hours at Milanello yesterday, after four at Casa Milan. The owner fully immersed himself in the Milan world again: he spoke with his transfer team, with the team about the match against Frosinone, and with Ruben Amorim about both topics.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

While Cardinale did not confirm the imminent arrival of Markus Krösche – though he did admit to being in talks with him – his clear intention is to build a top-tier organisation. Cardinale’s goal is to lead Milan to a trophy – ideally the Scudetto – as early as this season.

To do this, he knows strengthening the squad in January is a necessity. One name stands out in his notebook: Endrick, the forward currently with Real Madrid whom Mourinho – for the time being – is unwilling to let go of.

Regarding a potential move for the 20-year-old, Cardinale confirmed that the club like him: “Endrick’s name keeps coming up in the market. Our project goes beyond any single player, but Endrick is one of the best in the world – if not the best – considering his age and position. I have enormous respect for him, and we’ll see what might be possible.”

In other words, the green light would need to be secured from Mourinho regarding his departure from Madrid. Milan know they can leverage the strong relationship between its owner and Roc Nation, the agency representing the Brazilian.

Given the business already conducted between RedBird and Roc Nation, it is likely that the player would favour Milan over other potential destinations. Meanwhile, Tresoldi has also piqued Cardinale’s interest, though he offers a different profile than Endrick.

Nicolo Tresoldi is also an option for the attack, but more significant progress has been made regarding the Brazilian. Bayern Munich are also watching the Club Brugge striker, with Harry Kane having undergone ankle surgery.

In any case, Milan’s transfer activity will not be limited to a striker. Further arrivals will depend on the opportunities that arise during the winter window, with agents and intermediaries continually ringing the phone lines at Casa Milan.

There is a desire to bolster the defence, potentially with a central defender (possibly through the early return of Zachary Athekame, currently on loan at Lyon) and a left-sided player, should Pervis Estupiñán be sold.

All of this is in addition to the contract renewal for Rabiot, the next player set to be secured following the agreements reached with Strahinja Pavlović and Christian Pulišić. In short, there is a lot in the works.

#1767. Arsenal legend Alan Smith names two stars who could be sold to fund January spree

Arsenal great Alan Smith believes the Gunners will be tempted to cash in on Viktor Gyokeres and Martin Zubimendi when the January transfer opens.

The Premier League champions spent close to £200million bolstering their already formidable squad during the summer transfer window and are six points clear at the summit as they bid to hold onto their crown.

Arsenal signed Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge in the summer but failed to make any further additions in attack despite interest in Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez. While looking fearsome in all other departments, Arsenal’s forward line has still looked short on outstanding quality, not helped by Bukayo Saka’s absence with the winger expected to be sidelined until Christmas.

Gyokeres netted a wonderful strike in the Champions League against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday but is firmly second choice behind Kai Havertz in the league where he has started just one game this season.

The Sweden international recently played down talk of a mid-season move but former Gunners star Smith believes a sale could be considered at the Emirates if Arsenal find themselves needing to sell before they can buy in January.

Arsenal are interested in RB Leipzig star Antonio Nusa, with club legend Ian Wright telling the Gunners to go out and spend big on the Norway international. Bournemouth star Junior Kroupi is also firmly on their radar.

If it means funds for another recruit, Smith believes Arsenal will listen to offers for their striker.

‘Well, if it meant they could get somebody else in, I think you would,’ Smith told Metro when asked if Arsenal will listen to offers in January, speaking on behalf of Best Betting Sites.

‘He’s still a very sellable striker, I think. Other clubs would look at him and think he would fit into our style of play in a way that perhaps he doesn’t with Arsenal. And he showed with that goal last night that he’s still got something to offer. But on a consistent basis, it’s not been working for Arsenal.

‘So it’d be a good negotiating tool, I think, if you could do a swap, get somebody in and Gyokeres would go the other way.’

Zubimendi meanwhile was an almost ever-present figure in midfield last season following his £60million arrival from Real Sociedad but a draining season took its toll, ending the campaign on the bench with Myles Lewis-Skelly taking his place.

The Spain international is currently nursing a hamstring problem but has struggled for game time this season, starting just one match in the Premier League and Champions League.

Chelsea have been credited with interest in the 27-year-old with Smith believing he is likely be frustrated with his current role.

Asked if the Spaniard could be another who moves on in January, Smith said: ‘He might be. Zubimendi is probably getting a bit frustrated. He played so much when he first came, and maybe he was overplayed and began to look tired.

So it’s a bit of a conundrum, that one, whether Arteta’s decided he’s actually not the kind of midfield player he wants in there. He’s a world champion, he’s got great experience, you wouldn’t let him go lightly, but as things stand he’s on the fringes.’
